# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Operation Specifications
TerminalSokobanGame::run
Summary: The main game loop for the terminal-based runner. Renders the initial state, then repeatedly fetches an action, processes it, surfaces a status message to the user, and re-renders the board until the game ends.
Algorithm:
  1. renderingEngine.render(state).   // initial draw
  2. Loop:
       action = inputEngine.fetchAction().
       result = processAction(action).
       renderingEngine.message(formatMessage(result, state.getUndoQuota())).  // uses StringResources templates
       renderingEngine.render(state).
       if (shouldStop()) break;
  3. (Optional) render a final WIN_MESSAGE / goodbye line via renderingEngine.message(...).
Related Features: AbstractSokobanGame.state, AbstractSokobanGame.isExitSpecified, TerminalSokobanGame.inputEngine, TerminalSokobanGame.renderingEngine.
Related Classes: AbstractSokobanGame, SokobanGame, InputEngine, RenderingEngine, TerminalRenderingEngine, TerminalInputEngine, GameState, Action, ActionResult, StringResources.
Input: None (operates on injected state and engines).
Output: void - all visible output goes through the rendering engine.
Pre-condition: setState(GameState) has been called with a state containing at most two players (otherwise this runner throws IllegalArgumentException, as per the requirement); the input and rendering engines have been injected (typically by SokobanGameFactory).
Post-condition: The loop terminates when shouldStop() is true. No resources are left dangling if the JVM exits normally afterwards.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Operation Specifications
TerminalRenderingEngine::render
Summary: Writes an ASCII rendering of the supplied GameState to the configured output stream (typically System.out), drawing walls, floors, players, boxes, and destinations in a human-readable grid.
Algorithm:
  1. For y from 0 to state.boardHeight - 1:
       For x from 0 to state.boardWidth - 1:
         p = new Position(x, y); e = state.getEntity(p);
         Choose a single character:
            Wall         -> '#'
            Player p     -> Character.forDigit(p.id, 36) uppercased, or the literal upper-case letter; positions on a destination should typically be displayed with a marker (e.g. '+') but the exact choice is a presentation detail.
            Box b        -> Character.forDigit(b.playerId, 36) lowercased, again with marker ('*') when on a destination.
            Empty        -> '.' when on a destination, otherwise ' ' (space) or '.' per the chosen style.
       Print newline at the end of each row.
  2. Optionally print a status line (undo quota, etc.) using message(...) if design dictates; otherwise render() focuses solely on the board.
Related Features: TerminalRenderingEngine.outputStream.
Related Classes: PrintStream, GameState, Entity, Wall, Empty, Player, Box, Position, StringResources.
Input: state : GameState - a fully initialized state whose boardWidth and boardHeight are positive.
Output: void - text is written to the output stream.
Pre-condition: state is non-null and matches a valid map. The PrintStream is open.
Post-condition: The terminal shows the current board. No state in GameState is mutated.

```java
   *      b. Compute nextPosition = action.nextPosition(currentPosition).
   *      c. Resolve targetEntity = state.getEntity(nextPosition).
   *      d. If targetEntity is Empty: state.move(currentPosition, nextPosition); return Success.
   *      e. If targetEntity is a Box:
   *           i. If Box.playerId != action.initiator, return Failed("Cannot push other player's box").
   *           ii. Compute behindPosition = action.nextPosition(nextPosition).
   *           iii. If state.getEntity(behindPosition) is not Empty, return Failed("Box blocked").
   *           iv. state.move(currentPosition, nextPosition); state.move(nextPosition, behindPosition); state.checkpoint(); return Success.
   *      f. Otherwise (Wall, another Player, or unpushable Box): return Failed("Move blocked").
   *   2. If action is Undo:
   *      a. If state.undoQuota == 0, return Failed("Undo not allowed").
   *      b. If state.history is empty, return Failed("Nothing to undo").
   *      c. state.undo(); return Success.
   *   3. If action is Exit: set isExitSpecified = true; return Success.
   *   4. If action is InvalidInput: return Failed with the action's message.
   *   5. Default: return Failed("Unknown action").
   * Related Features: AbstractSokobanGame.isExitSpecified, AbstractSokobanGame.state.
   * Related Classes: GameState, Action, Move, Up, Down, Left, Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput, ActionResult, Success, Failed, Player, Box, Empty, Wall, Position.
   * Input: action : Action - the action to process (concrete subtype of Action: Move/Undo/Exit/InvalidInput). For Move/Undo, action.initiator must be a valid player id in [0, 25] that exists in the current state. For InvalidInput, action.initiator is -1. For Exit, action.initiator is irrelevant.
   * Output: ActionResult - either Success (no payload) or Failed carrying a human-readable reason String.
   * Pre-condition: state is a fully initialized, non-null GameState. For Move actions, the initiator player must currently exist on the board.
```

   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Dispatches a generic Action to its concrete handler and produces an ActionResult telling the caller (TerminalSokobanGame.run) whether the action was applied successfully or why it failed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If action is a Move:
   *      a. Determine initiator's current position via state.getPlayerPositionById(action.initiator). If not found, return Failed("Player not found").
   *      b. Compute nextPosition = action.nextPosition(currentPosition).
   *      c. Resolve targetEntity = state.getEntity(nextPosition).
   *      d. If targetEntity is Empty: state.move(currentPosition, nextPosition); return Success.
   *      e. If targetEntity is a Box:
   *           i. If Box.playerId != action.initiator, return Failed("Cannot push other player's box").
   *           ii. Compute behindPosition = action.nextPosition(nextPosition).
   *           iii. If state.getEntity(behindPosition) is not Empty, return Failed("Box blocked").
   *           iv. state.move(currentPosition, nextPosition); state.move(nextPosition, behindPosition); state.checkpoint(); return Success.
   *      f. Otherwise (Wall, another Player, or unpushable Box): return Failed("Move blocked").
   *   2. If action is Undo:
   *      a. If state.undoQuota == 0, return Failed("Undo not allowed").
   *      b. If state.history is empty, return Failed("Nothing to undo").
   *      c. state.undo(); return Success.
   *   3. If action is Exit: set isExitSpecified = true; return Success.
   *   4. If action is InvalidInput: return Failed with the action's message.
   *   5. Default: return Failed("Unknown action").
   * Related Features: AbstractSokobanGame.isExitSpecified, AbstractSokobanGame.state.
   * Related Classes: GameState, Action, Move, Up, Down, Left, Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput, ActionResult, Success, Failed, Player, Box, Empty, Wall, Position.
   * Input: action : Action - the action to process (concrete subtype of Action: Move/Undo/Exit/InvalidInput). For Move/Undo, action.initiator must be a valid player id in [0, 25] that exists in the current state. For InvalidInput, action.initiator is -1. For Exit, action.initiator is irrelevant.
   * Output: ActionResult - either Success (no payload) or Failed carrying a human-readable reason String.
   * Pre-condition: state is a fully initialized, non-null GameState. For Move actions, the initiator player must currently exist on the board.
   * Post-condition: If the returned ActionResult is Success and the action was a successful box-push Move, state.history contains a new checkpoint and state.undoQuota is unchanged; if the action was Undo with finite quota, state.undoQuota is decremented by one; if the action was Exit, AbstractSokobanGame.isExitSpecified == true. The board's invariant (one entity per cell, walls and destinations respected) is preserved.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public ActionResult processAction(final Action action)
  {
    Pa22Factory factory = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE;

    if (action instanceof Move)
    {
      Move moveAction = (Move) action;
      Position currentPosition = state.getPlayerPositionById(action.getInitiator());
      if (currentPosition == null)
      {
        Failed failed = factory.createFailed();
        failed.setReason("Player not found");
        return failed;
      }

      Position nextPosition = moveAction.nextPosition(currentPosition);
      Entity targetEntity = state.getEntity(nextPosition);

      if (targetEntity instanceof Empty)
      {
        state.move(currentPosition, nextPosition);
        return factory.createSuccess();
      }
      else if (targetEntity instanceof Box)
      {
        Box box = (Box) targetEntity;
        if (box.getPlayerId() != action.getInitiator())
        {
          Failed failed = factory.createFailed();
          failed.setReason("Cannot push other player's box");
          return failed;
        }

        Position behindPosition = moveAction.nextPosition(nextPosition);
        Entity behindEntity = state.getEntity(behindPosition);
        if (!(behindEntity instanceof Empty))
        {
          Failed failed = factory.createFailed();
          failed.setReason("Box blocked");
          return failed;
        }

        state.move(currentPosition, nextPosition);
        state.move(nextPosition, behindPosition);
        state.checkpoint();
        return factory.createSuccess();
      }
      else
      {
        Failed failed = factory.createFailed();
        failed.setReason("Move blocked");
        return failed;
      }
    }
    else if (action instanceof Undo)
    {
      if (state.getUndoQuota() == 0)
      {
        Failed failed = factory.createFailed();
        failed.setReason("Undo not allowed");
        return failed;
      }
      if (state.getHistory().isEmpty())
      {
        Failed failed = factory.createFailed();
        failed.setReason("Nothing to undo");
        return failed;
      }
      state.undo();
      return factory.createSuccess();
    }
    else if (action instanceof Exit)
    {
      setIsExitSpecified(true);
      return factory.createSuccess();
    }
    else if (action instanceof InvalidInput)
    {
      InvalidInput invalid = (InvalidInput) action;
      Failed failed = factory.createFailed();
      failed.setReason(invalid.getMessage());
      return failed;
    }
    else
    {
      Failed failed = factory.createFailed();
      failed.setReason("Unknown action");
      return failed;
    }
  }

```java
   * Algorithm:
```
```java
   *   1. If history is empty, return silently (no checkpoint exists; the caller is expected to guard). Undo is a no-op in this case.

   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
```
```java
   * Summary: Atomically relocates a single Entity from one cell to another on the live board and records the delta in the current transition so it can be checkpointed or undone later.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Bounds-check both from and to against boardWidth / boardHeight; throw if out of range.
   *   2. e = entities[from.y][from.x]. If e is null, throw IllegalStateException.
   *   3. entities[to.y][to.x] = e.
   *   4. entities[from.y][from.x] = Empty (the source cell is left empty after the entity leaves).
   *   5. currentTransition.add(from, to).
   * Related Features: GameState.entities, GameState.currentTransition.
   * Related Classes: EntityMap, Empty, GameStateTransition, Position.
   * Input: from : Position - source cell that must currently contain an Entity. to : Position - destination cell that the caller has already validated as empty (or that the caller is intentionally filling as part of a box-push sequence).
   * Output: void.

   * Summary: Reverts the board to the most recent checkpoint by atomically applying the reverse of every transition that has accumulated since that checkpoint, then pops the checkpoint off the history stack. Also decrements the finite undo quota when applicable.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If history is empty, return silently (no checkpoint exists; the caller is expected to guard). Undo is a no-op in this case.
   *   2. Pop the top TransitionStack entry, which represents the most recent checkpoint (ckpt).
   *   3. For every GameStateTransition t that was pushed on top of ckpt in reverse chronological order (i.e., the transitions accumulated since ckpt, popped in reverse order):
   *        let rev = t.reverse();
   *        for every (from, to) pair in rev: apply the move in reverse by swapping entities[from] and entities[to] so the board is rewound to the previous state.
   *   4. If undoQuota > 0, undoQuota-- (quota of -1 means unlimited and is not decremented; quota of 0 means undo is not allowed and the call is rejected by the caller).
   *   5. Reset currentTransition to a fresh empty GameStateTransition so the next round of moves starts a new delta.
   * Related Features: GameState.history, GameState.currentTransition, GameState.undoQuota.
   * Related Classes: GameStateTransition, TransitionStack, Position.
   * Input: None.
   * Output: void.
   * Pre-condition: history contains at least one checkpoint, and undoQuota != 0 (caller, processAction, enforces both). The transitions accumulated since the last checkpoint are intact and reconstructable.
   * Post-condition: The board exactly matches the state recorded at the popped checkpoint. The popped checkpoint (and any accumulated transitions since it) is removed from history. Finite undoQuota (when > 0) is decremented by 1. currentTransition is empty, ready to record the next set of moves.

   * Algorithm:
```

4. **isWin()**:
   - For every destination, check if entity is a Box

5. **getPlayerPositionById(int id)**:
   - Iterate entities, find Player with matching id

6. **getAllPlayerPositions()**:
   - Iterate entities, return list of positions where entity is Player

7. **getEntity(Position position)**:
   - Bounds check, return entity at position

Now let me think about the `undo` method's behavior more carefully. The docstring says:
- Pop the top TransitionStack entry (ckpt)
- For every GameStateTransition t that was pushed on top of ckpt (in reverse chronological order)
- Apply reverse of t

Wait, looking at the algorithm: "For every GameStateTransition t that was pushed on top of ckpt in reverse chronological order (i.e., the transitions accumulated since ckpt, popped in reverse order)"

This means after the checkpoint was pushed, subsequent transitions were also pushed. The undo should:
- Pop ckpt
- For each subsequent transition in reverse, reverse-apply it
- Decrement undoQuota

Wait, looking at the checkpoint algorithm: "push currentTransition onto history. Reset currentTransition to a fresh empty GameStateTransition". So the history stack contains multiple GameStateTransitions. The undo's algorithm makes more sense now: pop the top (latest checkpoint), then for any transitions pushed after it (until the next would-be checkpoint), apply their reverse in reverse order.

Let me re-read: "For every GameStateTransition t that was pushed on top of ckpt in reverse chronological order (i.e., the transitions accumulated since ckpt, popped in reverse order)"

So after popping ckpt, we then pop and reverse-apply other transitions that were pushed on top of ckpt. This is a single-level undo - just the most recent checkpoint and the transitions since it.

Actually, the simpler interpretation: pop top (ckpt) and stop. But the docstring says "transitions accumulated since ckpt" so there are more to undo. Let me apply all transitions popped until the history is empty (or until we encounter another "checkpoint" boundary, but we can't easily detect that).

Let me reconsider: "the transitions accumulated since ckpt" - the simplest interpretation is that we pop and reverse-apply all transitions until history is empty. But the algorithm says "in reverse chronological order" meaning we pop one at a time in LIFO order.

Let me look at this more carefully. The simplest and most reasonable implementation: pop ckpt, then for each remaining transition in history (popped in reverse order until empty), apply the reverse.

    while (!hist.isEmpty())
    {
      GameStateTransition t = hist.pop();
      GameStateTransition rev = t.reverse();
      Map<Position, Position> moves = rev.getMoves();
      if (moves != null)
      {
        for (Map.Entry<Position, Position> entry : moves.entrySet())
        {
          Position from = entry.getKey();
          Position to = entry.getValue();
          Entity eFrom = getEntities().get(from);
          Entity eTo = getEntities().get(to);
          getEntities().put(from, eTo);
          getEntities().put(to, eFrom);
        }
      }
    }

    if (getUndoQuota() > 0)
      setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);

    setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
  }

public void run()
{
  // 1. initial draw
  renderingEngine.render(getState());
  
  // 2. main loop
  while (true)
  {
    Action action = inputEngine.fetchAction();
    ActionResult result = processAction(action);
    
    int quota = getState() != null ? getState().getUndoQuota() : -1;
    renderingEngine.message(formatMessage(result, quota));
    renderingEngine.render(getState());
    
    if (shouldStop())
    {
      break;
    }
  }
  
  // 3. final goodbye line
  renderingEngine.message(StringResources.GAME_EXIT_MESSAGE);
}

private String formatMessage(ActionResult result, int undoQuota)
{
  String quotaDisplay = undoQuota < 0 ? StringResources.UNDO_QUOTA_UNLIMITED : Integer.toString(undoQuota);
  String template = String.format(StringResources.UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE, quotaDisplay);
  
  if (result == null)
  {
    return StringResources.INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE;
  }
  if (result instanceof Failed)
  {
    String reason = ((Failed) result).getReason();
    if (reason != null && !reason.isEmpty())
    {
      return reason.equals(StringResources.UNDO_QUOTA_RUN_OUT) ? reason : template;
    }
  }
  else if (result instanceof Success)
  {
    return template;
  }
  return template;
}

  }

  /**
   * Helper method to render a single entity.
   */
  private char renderEntity(Entity e, GameState state, Position p)
  {
    if (e instanceof Wall)
    {
      return '#';
    }
    else if (e instanceof Player)
    {

      int id = player.getId();
      return (char) ('A' + id);

    else if (e instanceof Box)

      return (char) ('a' + id);
    }
    else
    {

      {

      }
      return ' ';
    }

```java
                  entityMap.put(position, box);
                }
                break;
            }
          }
        }
    
        if (players.isEmpty())
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("no player");
        }
    
        if (destinations.size() != boxCount)
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("mismatch destinations");
        }
    
        if (!referencedPlayers.equals(players))
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("unmatched players");
        }
    
        GameMap gameMap = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameMap();
        gameMap.setMaxWidth(maxWidth);
        gameMap.setMaxHeight(maxHeight);
        gameMap.setUndoLimit(undoLimit);
        gameMap.getDestinations().addAll(destinations);
        gameMap.setMap(entityMap);
        return gameMap;
     
  }
```

6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;

8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

```text
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---

  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Operation Specifications
TerminalRenderingEngine::render
Summary: Renders the supplied GameState to the configured output stream
         (typically System.out) using text-based characters.
Algorithm:
  1. For y = 0 .. state.boardHeight - 1:
       a. For x = 0 .. state.boardWidth - 1:
             * e = state.getEntity(new Position(x, y))
             * Print the appropriate character:
                 - Wall        -> '#'
                 - Player i    -> (char)('A' + i)
                 - Box         -> (char)('a' + box.getPlayerId())
                 - Empty but destination -> '.'
                 - Empty       -> ' '
       b. Print a newline.
  2. Print extra information (e.g. undo quota, destinations remaining)
     after the board.
Related Features: outputStream
Related Classes: GameState, Entity, Wall, Player, Box, Empty, Position
Input: state : GameState - the dynamic state to display.
Output: void (text is written to outputStream).
Pre-condition: outputStream is open; state has been initialised.
Post-condition: The stream contains a fresh textual snapshot of the board.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

```text
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
```

# Operation Specifications
AbstractSokobanGame::shouldStop
Summary: Indicates whether the main game loop should terminate.
Algorithm:
  1. Return isExitSpecified == true OR state.isWin() == true.
Related Features: isExitSpecified, state
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the game loop should terminate, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: state has been initialised.
Post-condition: No state mutation.

AbstractSokobanGame::processAction
Summary: Processes a single Action supplied by the input engine and returns
         an ActionResult describing whether the action succeeded.
Algorithm:
  1. If action is null, return new Failed(new InvalidInput("null action")).
  2. Switch on the concrete type of action:
       a. Move (Up/Down/Left/Right):
            i.   player = state.getEntity(action.initiator's current position)
                 (resolve initiator -> Player position via
                  GameState.getAllPlayerPositions() / player id).
            ii.  nextPos = action.nextPosition(player.getPosition()).
            iii. Attempt to push/move via state.move(from, to).
            iv.  On success:
                  - if a box was pushed, call state.checkpoint()
                    and, if undoQuota != -1 and > 0, decrement undoQuota.
                  - return new Success(action).
            v.   On failure: return new Failed(action,
                  StringResources.MOVE_BLOCKED_MESSAGE).
       b. Undo:
            i.   If undoQuota == 0, return new Failed(action,
                  StringResources.NO_UNDO_QUOTA_MESSAGE).
            ii.  If state.history has no checkpoint, return
                  new Failed(action, StringResources.NOTHING_TO_UNDO_MESSAGE).
            iii. Apply state.undo() atomically (transition.reverse()).
            iv.  If undoQuota != -1, decrement undoQuota.
            v.   Return new Success(action).
       c. Exit:
            i.   Set isExitSpecified = true.
            ii.  Return new Success(action).
       d. InvalidInput:
            i.   Return new Failed(action, action.message).
  3. Return new Failed(action, "Unknown action").
Related Features: state, isExitSpecified
Related Classes: Action, ActionResult, Success, Failed, Move, Up, Down, Left,
                 Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput, GameState,
                 StringResources
Input: action : Action - the action to be processed; must not be null.
Output: ActionResult - Success or Failed wrapping the original action and
        (for Failed) a human-readable reason.
Pre-condition: state has been initialised via setState(GameState) and
               action.initiator references a valid player (or -1 for
               InvalidInput).
Post-condition: The game state reflects the executed action; undoQuota is
                decremented only when an undo actually consumes a
                checkpoint; for Exit actions isExitSpecified is true.

# Operation Specifications
AbstractSokobanGame::shouldStop
Summary: Indicates whether the main game loop should terminate.
Algorithm:
  1. Return isExitSpecified == true OR state.isWin() == true.
Related Features: isExitSpecified, state
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the game loop should terminate, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: state has been initialised.
Post-condition: No state mutation.

AbstractSokobanGame::processAction
Summary: Processes a single Action supplied by the input engine and returns
         an ActionResult describing whether the action succeeded.
Algorithm:
  1. If action is null, return new Failed(new InvalidInput("null action")).
  2. Switch on the concrete type of action:
       a. Move (Up/Down/Left/Right):
            i.   player = state.getEntity(action.initiator's current position)
                 (resolve initiator -> Player position via
                  GameState.getAllPlayerPositions() / player id).
            ii.  nextPos = action.nextPosition(player.getPosition()).
            iii. Attempt to push/move via state.move(from, to).
            iv.  On success:
                  - if a box was pushed, call state.checkpoint()
                    and, if undoQuota != -1 and > 0, decrement undoQuota.
                  - return new Success(action).
            v.   On failure: return new Failed(action,
                  StringResources.MOVE_BLOCKED_MESSAGE).
       b. Undo:
            i.   If undoQuota == 0, return new Failed(action,
                  StringResources.NO_UNDO_QUOTA_MESSAGE).
            ii.  If state.history has no checkpoint, return
                  new Failed(action, StringResources.NOTHING_TO_UNDO_MESSAGE).
            iii. Apply state.undo() atomically (transition.reverse()).
            iv.  If undoQuota != -1, decrement undoQuota.
            v.   Return new Success(action).
       c. Exit:
            i.   Set isExitSpecified = true.
            ii.  Return new Success(action).
       d. InvalidInput:
            i.   Return new Failed(action, action.message).
  3. Return new Failed(action, "Unknown action").
Related Features: state, isExitSpecified
Related Classes: Action, ActionResult, Success, Failed, Move, Up, Down, Left,
                 Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput, GameState,
                 StringResources
Input: action : Action - the action to be processed; must not be null.
Output: ActionResult - Success or Failed wrapping the original action and
        (for Failed) a human-readable reason.
Pre-condition: state has been initialised via setState(GameState) and
               action.initiator references a valid player (or -1 for
               InvalidInput).
Post-condition: The game state reflects the executed action; undoQuota is
                decremented only when an undo actually consumes a
                checkpoint; for Exit actions isExitSpecified is true.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Operation Specifications
GameMap::getPlayerIds
Summary: Returns the set of player identifiers present on the static map
         (used by the parser/validator to ensure box/player correspondence).
Algorithm:
  1. Iterate the entities stored in map (EntityMap).
  2. For every Entity that is a Player, collect its id.
  3. Return the collected list preserving discovery order.
Related Features: map (EntityMap)
Related Classes: EntityMap, Player, EIntegerObject
Input: none
Output: List<EIntegerObject> - non-empty list of unique player IDs contained
        on the map (one entry per player).
Pre-condition: The map has been initialised through PA22Helper.parseGameMap
               and validated to contain at least one player.
Post-condition: The returned list is a snapshot; modifying it does not
                alter the underlying map.

GameMap::putEntity
Summary: Places an Entity at the supplied position on the static map.
         Used primarily by the parser to populate the board.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate position is within [0, maxWidth) and [0, maxHeight).
  2. Store the entity in the internal EntityMap at the given key.
Related Features: map, maxWidth, maxHeight
Related Classes: Entity, EntityMap, Position
Input:
  - position : Position - the target cell; must lie within the map bounds.
  - entity   : Entity   - the entity to place (Player, Box, Wall, Empty...).
Output: void
Pre-condition: 0 <= position.x < maxWidth and 0 <= position.y < maxHeight;
               entity != null.
Post-condition: The EntityMap now associates `position` with `entity`,
                replacing any previous occupant.

# Operation Specifications
GameMap::getPlayerIds
Summary: Returns the set of player identifiers present on the static map
         (used by the parser/validator to ensure box/player correspondence).
Algorithm:
  1. Iterate the entities stored in map (EntityMap).
  2. For every Entity that is a Player, collect its id.
  3. Return the collected list preserving discovery order.
Related Features: map (EntityMap)
Related Classes: EntityMap, Player, EIntegerObject
Input: none
Output: List<EIntegerObject> - non-empty list of unique player IDs contained
        on the map (one entry per player).
Pre-condition: The map has been initialised through PA22Helper.parseGameMap
               and validated to contain at least one player.
Post-condition: The returned list is a snapshot; modifying it does not
                alter the underlying map.

GameMap::putEntity
Summary: Places an Entity at the supplied position on the static map.
         Used primarily by the parser to populate the board.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate position is within [0, maxWidth) and [0, maxHeight).
  2. Store the entity in the internal EntityMap at the given key.
Related Features: map, maxWidth, maxHeight
Related Classes: Entity, EntityMap, Position
Input:
  - position : Position - the target cell; must lie within the map bounds.
  - entity   : Entity   - the entity to place (Player, Box, Wall, Empty...).
Output: void
Pre-condition: 0 <= position.x < maxWidth and 0 <= position.y < maxHeight;
               entity != null.
Post-condition: The EntityMap now associates `position` with `entity`,
                replacing any previous occupant.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```
