# Operation Specifications
TerminalInputEngine::fetchAction
Summary: Reads a single line of input from the terminal and converts it
         into a concrete Action instance (Move/Undo/Exit/InvalidInput).
Algorithm:
  1. If terminalScanner has no more input, return new Exit().
  2. line = terminalScanner.nextLine().trim().toLowerCase().
  3. Switch on line:
       a. "w" -> return new Up(0)
       b. "s" -> return new Down(0)
       c. "a" -> return new Left(0)
       d. "d" -> return new Right(0)
       e. "k" -> return new Up(1)
       f. "j" -> return new Down(1)
       g. "h" -> return new Left(1)
       h. "l" -> return new Right(1)
       i. "r" -> return new Undo(0)
       j. "u" -> return new Undo(1)
       k. "exit" -> return new Exit()
       l. default -> return new InvalidInput(-1,
                 StringResources.INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE)
Related Features: terminalScanner
Related Classes: Action, Move, Up, Down, Left, Right, Undo, Exit,
                 InvalidInput, StringResources
Input: None (reads one line from the standard input via terminalScanner).
Output: Action - the parsed action with the appropriate initiator id.
Pre-condition: terminalScanner is initialised and bound to an open input
               source.
Post-condition: One line of input has been consumed; the next call will
                read the following line.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Operation Specifications
TerminalSokobanGame::run
Summary: Drives the terminal-based main game loop: renders the initial
         state, repeatedly fetches an action from the input engine,
         processes it, prints a status message, renders the updated state,
         and stops when shouldStop() returns true.
Algorithm:
  1. renderingEngine.render(state)  // initial board
  2. Loop:
       a. action = inputEngine.fetchAction().
       b. result = processAction(action).
       c. renderingEngine.message(result.toString()).
       d. renderingEngine.render(state).
       e. If shouldStop() is true, break.
  3. (Optional) print final message via renderingEngine.message(...).
Related Features: inputEngine, renderingEngine, state
Related Classes: GameState, Action, ActionResult, InputEngine, RenderingEngine
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: setState(GameState) has been called with a state containing
               at most two players; inputEngine and renderingEngine are
               configured.
Post-condition: The terminal displays the full play-through up to the point
                where shouldStop() became true; the exit flag or win
                condition terminates the loop.

```text
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

Related Features: none

Output: Position - the adjacent cell located one row below.
Pre-condition: currentPosition != null; (no constraint on bounds - the
               caller verifies whether the position lies inside the board).
Post-condition: A new Position object is returned; the input is not mutated.

# Operation Specifications
GameState::undo
Summary: Reverts the most recent checkpointed transition atomically so that
         all entities return to their pre-push positions.
Algorithm:
  1. If history is empty, do nothing (or signal no-op).
  2. Pop the most recent GameStateTransition from history.
  3. Call transition.reverse() and apply the reversed move map to entities
     via entities.moveAll(reverse) (or per-entry entities.move(to, from)).
  4. Clear currentTransition.
Related Features: entities, history, currentTransition
Related Classes: GameStateTransition, EntityMap, Position
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: history contains at least one checkpoint; undoQuota is not
               already 0 (checked by caller).
Post-condition: All entities are restored to their positions prior to the
                most recent box-push checkpoint; currentTransition is reset.

GameState::isWin
Summary: Determines whether the current board satisfies the win condition
         (every destination is occupied by a Box).
Algorithm:
  1. For each destination position p in destinations:
       a. e = entities.getEntity(p).
       b. If e is not a Box, return false.
  2. Return true.
Related Features: destinations, entities
Related Classes: Box, Entity, Position
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if every destination is currently occupied by a Box.
Pre-condition: destinations is non-empty and entities has been initialised.
Post-condition: No state mutation.

GameState::checkpoint
Summary: Records the current move transition as a checkpoint in the undo
         history so that it can be reverted by undo().
Algorithm:
  1. If currentTransition is null or contains no moves, do nothing.
  2. Push currentTransition onto history.
  3. Create a fresh empty GameStateTransition and assign it to
     currentTransition.
Related Features: history, currentTransition
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: currentTransition has been populated with the moves performed
               during the most recent successful push.
Post-condition: The previous transition is available in history for
                potential undo; a new empty transition is active.

GameState::move
Summary: Attempts to move the entity located at `from` to `to`, pushing a
         Box one cell further when applicable; records the resulting moves
         in currentTransition.
Algorithm:
  1. e = entities.getEntity(from). If null, fail (return false / throw).
  2. occupant = entities.getEntity(to).
  3. If occupant is a Wall or another Player, fail.
  4. If occupant is an Empty:
       a. entities.move(from, to).
       b. currentTransition.add(from, to).
  5. If occupant is a Box:
       a. The box must belong to the moving player: box.playerId ==
          player.id, else fail.
       b. Compute the cell behind the box (beyond `to`, in the same
          direction).
       c. behind = entities.getEntity(behindPos). If behind is not Empty,
          fail.
       d. entities.move(to, behindPos)  // push the box
       e. entities.move(from, to)        // move the player
       f. currentTransition.add(from, to) and currentTransition.add(to,
          behindPos).
  6. Return true on success.
Related Features: entities, currentTransition
Related Classes: Entity, Wall, Player, Box, Empty, Position,
                 GameStateTransition
Input:
  - from : Position - the cell currently occupied by the moving player;
          must be a valid in-bounds position containing a Player.
  - to   : Position - the desired destination cell; must be in bounds.
Output: boolean - true if the move (and any push) succeeded, false
        otherwise.
Pre-condition: from and to are in bounds; entities has been initialised;
               the player at `from` owns any box at `to`.
Post-condition: On success, entities and currentTransition are updated to
                reflect the move and (if any) the pushed box; on failure,
                no state is mutated.

GameState::getPlayerPositionById
Summary: Returns the board cell occupied by the player with the supplied id.
Algorithm:
  1. Iterate entities; for each Player whose id matches, return its position.
  2. If no match is found, return null (caller must handle gracefully).
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: EntityMap, Player, Position
Input: id : int - the player identifier (0..25).
Output: Position - the cell currently holding the matching player, or null
        when the id is unknown.
Pre-condition: The id refers to a player that exists in the current state.
Post-condition: No side effects.

GameState::getAllPlayerPositions
Summary: Returns the on-board positions of every Player currently alive
         in the dynamic state.
Algorithm:
  1. Walk the entities map.
  2. For every Entity that is a Player, record its (x, y) coordinate.
  3. Return the collected list.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: EntityMap, Player, Position
Input: none
Output: List<Position> - one Position per Player present on the board; the
        list is empty only when no player exists (should not occur in a
        valid game).
Pre-condition: The state has been initialised.
Post-condition: Returned list is a snapshot, no mutation of state.

GameState::getEntity
Summary: Retrieves the Entity currently occupying a given cell.
Algorithm:
  1. If the position is out of board bounds, return null (or a Wall
     equivalent) so the caller treats it as blocked.
  2. Return entities.get(position); may return null for off-grid lookups.
Related Features: entities, boardWidth, boardHeight
Related Classes: EntityMap, Entity, Position
Input: position : Position - the cell to query.
Output: Entity - the occupant of that cell, or null if the cell is empty
        / off the board.
Pre-condition: state initialised.
Post-condition: No side effects; underlying entities map is not modified.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pesudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.

3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Operation Specifications
GameState::undo
Summary: Reverts the most recent checkpointed transition atomically so that
         all entities return to their pre-push positions.
Algorithm:
  1. If history is empty, do nothing (no-op).
  2. Pop the most recent GameStateTransition from history.
  3. Call transition.reverse() and apply the reversed move map to entities
     (e.g., for each entry in the reversed move map, entities.move(to, from)).
  4. Clear currentTransition.
Related Features: entities, history, currentTransition
Related Classes: GameStateTransition, EntityMap, Position
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: history contains at least one checkpoint; undoQuota is not
               already 0 (checked by caller); a finite undoQuota is consumed
               only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
Post-condition: All entities are restored to their positions prior to the
                most recent box-push checkpoint; currentTransition is reset.

GameState::isWin
Summary: Determines whether the current board satisfies the win condition
         (every destination is occupied by a Box).
Algorithm:
  1. For each destination position p in destinations:
       a. e = entities.getEntity(p).
       b. If e is not a Box, return false.
  2. Return true.
Related Features: destinations, entities
Related Classes: Box, Entity, Position
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if every destination is currently occupied by a Box.
Pre-condition: entities has been initialised.
Post-condition: No state mutation.

GameState::checkpoint
Summary: Records the current move transition as a checkpoint in the undo
         history so that it can be reverted by undo(). A checkpoint is
         recorded when a box is successfully pushed.
Algorithm:
  1. If currentTransition is null or contains no moves, do nothing.
  2. Push currentTransition onto history.
  3. Create a fresh empty GameStateTransition and assign it to
     currentTransition.
Related Features: history, currentTransition
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: currentTransition has been populated with the moves performed
               during the most recent successful push.
Post-condition: The previous transition is available in history for
                potential undo; a new empty transition is active.

GameState::move
Summary: Attempts to move the entity located at `from` to `to`, pushing a
         Box one cell further when applicable; records the resulting moves
         in currentTransition.
Algorithm:
  1. e = entities.getEntity(from). If null, fail (return false).
  2. occupant = entities.getEntity(to).
  3. If occupant is a Wall or another Player, fail.
  4. If occupant is an Empty:
       a. entities.move(from, to).
       b. currentTransition.add(from, to).
  5. If occupant is a Box:
       a. The box must belong to the moving player: box.playerId ==
          player.id, else fail.
       b. Compute the cell behind the box (beyond `to`, in the same
          direction).
       c. behind = entities.getEntity(behindPos). If behind is not Empty,
          fail.
       d. entities.move(to, behindPos)  // push the box
       e. entities.move(from, to)        // move the player
       f. currentTransition.add(from, to) and currentTransition.add(to,
          behindPos).
  6. Return true on success.
Related Features: entities, currentTransition
Related Classes: Entity, Wall, Player, Box, Empty, Position,
                 GameStateTransition
Input:
  - from : Position - the cell currently occupied by the moving player;
          must be a valid in-bounds position containing a Player.
  - to   : Position - the desired destination cell; must be in bounds.
Output: boolean - true if the move (and any push) succeeded, false
        otherwise.
Pre-condition: from and to are in bounds; entities has been initialised;
               the player at `from` owns any box at `to`; the space behind
               the box is empty if a push is attempted.
Post-condition: On success, entities and currentTransition are updated to
                reflect the move and (if any) the pushed box; on failure,
                no state is mutated.

GameState::getPlayerPositionById
Summary: Returns the board cell occupied by the player with the supplied id.
Algorithm:
  1. Iterate entities; for each Player whose id matches, return its position.
  2. If no match is found, return null (caller must handle gracefully).
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: EntityMap, Player, Position
Input: id : int - the player identifier (0..25).
Output: Position - the cell currently holding the matching player, or null
        when the id is unknown.
Pre-condition: The state has been initialised.
Post-condition: No side effects.

GameState::getAllPlayerPositions
Summary: Returns the on-board positions of every Player currently in
         the dynamic state.
Algorithm:
  1. Walk the entities map.
  2. For every Entity that is a Player, record its (x, y) coordinate.
  3. Return the collected list.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: EntityMap, Player, Position
Input: None
Output: List<Position> - one Position per Player present on the board; the
        list is empty only when no player exists.
Pre-condition: The state has been initialised.
Post-condition: Returned list is a snapshot, no mutation of state.

GameState::getEntity
Summary: Retrieves the Entity currently occupying a given cell.
Algorithm:
  1. If the position is out of board bounds, return null so the caller
     treats it as blocked.
  2. Return entities.get(position); may return null for empty cells.
Related Features: entities, boardWidth, boardHeight
Related Classes: EntityMap, Entity, Position
Input: position : Position - the cell to query.
Output: Entity - the occupant of that cell, or null if the cell is empty
        / off the board.
Pre-condition: state initialised.
Post-condition: No side effects; underlying entities map is not modified.

  4. Clear currentTransition.
Related Features: entities, history, currentTransition
Related Classes: GameStateTransition, EntityMap, Position
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: history contains at least one checkpoint; undoQuota is not
               already 0 (checked by caller); a finite undoQuota is consumed
               only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
Post-condition: All entities are restored to their positions prior to the
                most recent box-push checkpoint; currentTransition is reset.

GameState::isWin
Summary: Determines whether the current board satisfies the win condition
         (every destination is occupied by a Box).
Algorithm:
  1. For each destination position p in destinations:
       a. e = entities.getEntity(p).
       b. If e is not a Box, return false.
  2. Return true.
Related Features: destinations, entities
Related Classes: Box, Entity, Position
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if every destination is currently occupied by a Box.
Pre-condition: entities has been initialised.
Post-condition: No state mutation.

GameState::checkpoint
Summary: Records the current move transition as a checkpoint in the undo
         history so that it can be reverted by undo(). A checkpoint is
         recorded when a box is successfully pushed.
Algorithm:
  1. If currentTransition is null or contains no moves, do nothing.
  2. Push currentTransition onto history.
  3. Create a fresh empty GameStateTransition and assign it to
     currentTransition.
Related Features: history, currentTransition
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: currentTransition has been populated with the moves performed
               during the most recent successful push.
Post-condition: The previous transition is available in history for
                potential undo; a new empty transition is active.

GameState::move
Summary: Attempts to move the entity located at `from` to `to`, pushing a
         Box one cell further when applicable; records the resulting moves
         in currentTransition.
Algorithm:
  1. e = entities.getEntity(from). If null, fail (return false).
  2. occupant = entities.getEntity(to).
  3. If occupant is a Wall or another Player, fail.
  4. If occupant is an Empty:
       a. entities.move(from, to).
       b. currentTransition.add(from, to).
  5. If occupant is a Box:
       a. The box must belong to the moving player: box.playerId ==
          player.id, else fail.
       b. Compute the cell behind the box (beyond `to`, in the same
          direction).
       c. behind = entities.getEntity(behindPos). If behind is not Empty,
          fail.
       d. entities.move(to, behindPos)  // push the box
       e. entities.move(from, to)        // move the player
       f. currentTransition.add(from, to) and currentTransition.add(to,
          behindPos).
  6. Return true on success.
Related Features: entities, currentTransition
Related Classes: Entity, Wall, Player, Box, Empty, Position,
                 GameStateTransition
Input:
  - from : Position - the cell currently occupied by the moving player;
          must be a valid in-bounds position containing a Player.
  - to   : Position - the desired destination cell; must be in bounds.
Output: boolean - true if the move (and any push) succeeded, false
        otherwise.
Pre-condition: from and to are in bounds; entities has been initialised;
               the player at `from` owns any box at `to`; the space behind
               the box is empty if a push is attempted.
Post-condition: On success, entities and currentTransition are updated to
                reflect the move and (if any) the pushed box; on failure,
                no state is mutated.

GameState::getPlayerPositionById
Summary: Returns the board cell occupied by the player with the supplied id.
Algorithm:
  1. Iterate entities; for each Player whose id matches, return its position.
  2. If no match is found, return null (caller must handle gracefully).
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: EntityMap, Player, Position
Input: id : int - the player identifier (0..25).
Output: Position - the cell currently holding the matching player, or null
        when the id is unknown.
Pre-condition: The state has been initialised.
Post-condition: No side effects.

GameState::getAllPlayerPositions
Summary: Returns the on-board positions of every Player currently in
         the dynamic state.
Algorithm:
  1. Walk the entities map.
  2. For every Entity that is a Player, record its (x, y) coordinate.
  3. Return the collected list.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: EntityMap, Player, Position
Input: None
Output: List<Position> - one Position per Player present on the board; the
        list is empty only when no player exists.
Pre-condition: The state has been initialised.
Post-condition: Returned list is a snapshot, no mutation of state.

GameState::getEntity
Summary: Retrieves the Entity currently occupying a given cell.
Algorithm:
  1. If the position is out of board bounds, return null so the caller
     treats it as blocked.
  2. Return entities.get(position); may return null for empty cells.
Related Features: entities, boardWidth, boardHeight
Related Classes: EntityMap, Entity, Position
Input: position : Position - the cell to query.
Output: Entity - the occupant of that cell, or null if the cell is empty
        / off the board.
Pre-condition: state initialised.
Post-condition: No side effects; underlying entities map is not modified.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

```java
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Processes a single Action supplied by the input engine and returns
   *          an ActionResult describing whether the action succeeded.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If action is null, return new Failed(new InvalidInput("null action")).
   *   2. Switch on the concrete type of action:
   *        a. Move (Up/Down/Left/Right):
   *             i.   currentPos = state.getPlayerPositionById(action.initiator).
   *                  (Resolve the initiator's current position via GameState; the
   *                  Player is an Entity and does not expose a getPosition() method.)
   *             ii.  nextPos = action.nextPosition(currentPos).
   *             iii. Attempt to push/move via state.move(currentPos, nextPos).
   *             iv.  On success:
   *                   - if a box was pushed, call state.checkpoint().
   *                     (The undoQuota is NOT decremented here; finite quota is
   *                      consumed only by Undo actions that pop a checkpoint.)
   *                   - return new Success(action).
   *             v.   On failure: return new Failed(action,
   *                   StringResources.MOVE_BLOCKED_MESSAGE).
   *        b. Undo:
   *             i.   If undoQuota == 0, return new Failed(action,
   *                   StringResources.NO_UNDO_QUOTA_MESSAGE).
   *             ii.  If state.history has no checkpoint to pop, return
   *                   new Failed(action, StringResources.NOTHING_TO_UNDO_MESSAGE).
   *             iii. Apply state.undo() atomically (currentTransition.reverse()).
   *             iv.  If undoQuota != -1 (i.e. finite quota), decrement undoQuota.
   *             v.   Return new Success(action).
   *        c. Exit:
   *             i.   Set isExitSpecified = true.
   *             ii.  Return new Success(action).
   *        d. InvalidInput:
   *             i.   Return new Failed(action, action.message).
   *   3. Return new Failed(action, "Unknown action").
   * Related Features: state, isExitSpecified, undoQuota
   * Related Classes: Action, ActionResult, Success, Failed, Move, Up, Down, Left,
   *                  Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput, GameState, Position,
   *                  StringResources
   * Input: action : Action - the action to be processed; must not be null.
   * Output: ActionResult - Success or Failed wrapping the original action and
   *         (for Failed) a human-readable reason.
   * Pre-condition: state has been initialised via setState(GameState). The
   *                caller may supply any Action produced by the input engine
   *                (including InvalidInput with initiator = -1, or actions
   *                whose initiator does not match a current player); such
   *                cases are handled by returning a Failed result.
   * Post-condition: The game state reflects the executed action. undoQuota is
   *                 decremented only when an Undo action actually consumes a
   *                 checkpoint (and never decremented by Move actions). For
```

```java
   *                caller may supply any Action produced by the input engine
   *                (including InvalidInput with initiator = -1, or actions
   *                whose initiator does not match a current player); such
   *                cases are handled by returning a Failed result.
   * Post-condition: The game state reflects the executed action. undoQuota is
   *                 decremented only when an Undo action actually consumes a
   *                 checkpoint (and never decremented by Move actions). For
   *                 Exit actions isExitSpecified is true.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
```
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public ActionResult processAction(final Action action)
  {
    if (action == null)
    {
      InvalidInput invalid = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createInvalidInput();
      invalid.setMessage("null action");
      Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
      failed.setAction(invalid);
      failed.setReason("null action");
      return failed;
    }

    if (action instanceof Move)
    {
      Move move = (Move) action;
      Position currentPos = state.getPlayerPositionById(action.getInitiator());
      Position nextPos = move.nextPosition(currentPos);
      Entity entityAtNext = state.getEntity(nextPos);
      if (entityAtNext instanceof Wall)
      {
        Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
        failed.setAction(action);
        failed.setReason(StringResources.MOVE_BLOCKED_MESSAGE);
        return failed;
      }
      boolean boxPushed = entityAtNext instanceof Box;
      state.move(currentPos, nextPos);
      if (boxPushed)
      {
        state.checkpoint();
      }
      Success success = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
      success.setAction(action);
      return success;
    }
    else if (action instanceof Undo)
    {
      if (state.getUndoQuota() == 0)
      {
        Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
        failed.setAction(action);
        failed.setReason(StringResources.NO_UNDO_QUOTA_MESSAGE);
        return failed;
      }
      if (state.getHistory() == null || state.getHistory().isEmpty())
      {
        Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
        failed.setAction(action);
        failed.setReason(StringResources.NOTHING_TO_UNDO_MESSAGE);
        return failed;
      }
      state.undo();
      if (state.getUndoQuota() != -1)
      {
        state.setUndoQuota(state.getUndoQuota() - 1);
      }
      Success success = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
      success.setAction(action);
      return success;
    }
    else if (action instanceof Exit)
    {
      setIsExitSpecified(true);
      Success success = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
      success.setAction(action);
      return success;
    }
    else if (action instanceof InvalidInput)
    {
      Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
      failed.setAction(action);
      failed.setReason(((InvalidInput) action).getMessage());
      return failed;
    }

    Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
    failed.setAction(action);
    failed.setReason("Unknown action");
    return failed;
  }

```java
   * Summary: Attempts to move the entity located at `from` to `to`, pushing a
   *          Box one cell further when applicable; records the resulting moves
   *          in currentTransition.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. e = entities.getEntity(from). If null, fail (return false).
   *   2. occupant = entities.getEntity(to).
   *   3. If occupant is a Wall, another Player, or an unpushable Box

   *   4. If occupant is an Empty:
```

```java
   * Summary: Attempts to move the entity located at `from` to `to`, pushing a

   *          in currentTransition.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. e = entities.getEntity(from). If null, fail (return false).
```

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Attempts to move the entity located at `from` to `to`, pushing a
   *          Box one cell further when applicable; records the resulting moves
   *          in currentTransition.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. e = entities.getEntity(from). If null, fail (return false).
   *   2. occupant = entities.getEntity(to).
   *   3. If occupant is a Wall, another Player, or an unpushable Box
   *      (Box whose playerId does not match the moving player's id), fail.
   *   4. If occupant is an Empty:
   *        a. entities.move(from, to).
   *        b. currentTransition.add(from, to).
   *   5. If occupant is a pushable Box (Box.playerId matches the moving
   *      player's id):
   *        a. Compute the cell behind the box (beyond `to`, in the same
   *           direction).
   *        b. behind = entities.getEntity(behindPos). If behind is not Empty,
   *           fail.
   *        c. entities.move(to, behindPos)  // push the box
   *        d. entities.move(from, to)        // move the player
   *        e. currentTransition.add(from, to) and currentTransition.add(to,
   *           behindPos).
   *   6. Return true on success.
   * Related Features: entities, currentTransition
   * Related Classes: Entity, Wall, Player, Box, Empty, Position,
   *                  GameStateTransition
   * Input:
   *   - from : Position - the cell currently occupied by the moving player;
   *           must be a valid in-bounds position containing a Player.
   *   - to   : Position - the desired destination cell; must be in bounds.
   *   - player : Player - the player performing the move; used to validate
   *              box ownership when a push is attempted. The caller supplies
   *              the Player located at `from`.
   * Output: boolean - true if the move (and any push) succeeded, false
   *         otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: from and to are in bounds; entities has been initialised;
   *                the player supplied as the moving entity owns any box at
   *                `to`; the space behind the box is empty if a push is
   *                attempted.
   * Post-condition: On success, entities and currentTransition are updated to
   *                 reflect the move and (if any) the pushed box; on failure,
   *                 no state is mutated.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void move(final Position from, final Position to)
  {
    Entity e = getEntity(from);
    if (e == null) {
      return;
    }
    Entity occupant = getEntity(to);
    if (occupant == null) {
      return;
    }
    if (occupant instanceof Wall || occupant instanceof Player) {
      return;
    }
    if (occupant instanceof Box) {
      Box box = (Box) occupant;
      if (e instanceof Player) {
        if (box.getPlayerId() != ((Player) e).getId()) {
          return;
        }
      } else {
        return;
      }
    }
    if (occupant instanceof Empty) {
      entities.remove(from);
      entities.put(to, e);
      getCurrentTransition().add(from, to);
    } else if (occupant instanceof Box) {
      int dx = to.getX() - from.getX();
      int dy = to.getY() - from.getY();
      Position behindPos = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createPosition();
      behindPos.setX(to.getX() + dx);
      behindPos.setY(to.getY() + dy);
      Entity behind = getEntity(behindPos);
      if (behind == null || !(behind instanceof Empty)) {
        return;
      }
      Entity boxEntity = entities.remove(to);
      entities.put(behindPos, boxEntity);
      entities.remove(from);
      entities.put(to, e);
      getCurrentTransition().add(from, to);
      getCurrentTransition().add(to, behindPos);
    }
  }

   * Summary: Reverts the most recent checkpointed transition atomically so that

   * Algorithm:

   *   2. Pop the most recent GameStateTransition from history.
   *   3. Call transition.reverse() and apply the reversed move map to entities

   *   4. Clear currentTransition.
   *   5. If undoQuota is a finite non-negative value, decrement it by 1.
   *      (undoQuota == -1 means unlimited and is not decremented; undoQuota == 0
   *      means undo is not allowed and this method is not invoked by the caller.)
   * Related Features: entities, history, currentTransition, undoQuota
   * Related Classes: GameStateTransition, EntityMap, Position

   *                the caller (caller ensures this).
   * Post-condition: All entities are restored to their positions prior to the
   *                 most recent box-push checkpoint; currentTransition is reset;
   *                 finite undoQuota is decremented by 1; -1 (unlimited) is

   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT

  public void undo()
  {
    if (getHistory().isEmpty()) {
      return;
    }
    GameStateTransition last = getHistory().pop();
    GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
    Map<Position, Position> reversedMoves = reversed.getMoves();
    for (Map.Entry<Position, Position> entry : reversedMoves.entrySet()) {
      Position to = entry.getKey();
      Position from = entry.getValue();
      Entity ent = entities.remove(to);
      if (ent != null) {
        entities.put(from, ent);
      }
    }
    setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
    if (getUndoQuota() >= 0) {
      setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);
    }
  }

public void render(final GameState state)
{
    if (outputStream == null)
    {
        throw new UnsupportedOperationException();
    }
    java.util.Set<Position> destinationSet = new java.util.HashSet<Position>(state.getDestinations());
    for (int y = 0; y < state.getBoardHeight(); y++)
    {
        for (int x = 0; x < state.getBoardWidth(); x++)
        {
            Position p = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createPosition();
            p.setX(x);
            p.setY(y);
            Entity e = state.getEntity(p);
            char c;
            if (e instanceof Wall)
            {
                c = '#';
            }
            else if (e instanceof Player)
            {
                c = (char) ('A' + ((Player) e).getId());
            }
            else if (e instanceof Box)
            {
                c = (char) ('a' + ((Box) e).getPlayerId());
            }
            else if (e instanceof Empty)
            {
                if (destinationSet.contains(p))
                {
                    c = '.';
                }
                else
                {
                    c = ' ';
                }
            }
            else
            {
                c = ' ';
            }
            outputStream.print(c);
        }
        outputStream.println();
    }
    // Extra information
    outputStream.println("Undo quota: " + state.getUndoQuota());
    outputStream.println("Destinations remaining: " + state.getDestinations().size());
}

Complete this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Compute context information
  1.1 Navigate the Ecore model to find related classes
  1.2 Also consider the related classes in the Javadocs.
  1.3 Locate these files in your project.
  1.4 Generate the class summarization.
2. Read the error messages carefully.
3. Do your best to fix the errors locally without introducing new types, fields, and methods.
4. You should not remove faulty methods to eliminate compilation errors.
5. Do not change parts without errors.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

```java
      return success;
```

   *                   new Failed(action, StringResources.NOTHING_TO_UNDO_MESSAGE).
   *             iii. Apply state.undo() atomically (currentTransition.reverse()).
   *             iv.  If undoQuota != -1 (i.e. finite quota), decrement undoQuota.
   *             v.   Return new Success(action).
   *        c. Exit:
   *             i.   Set isExitSpecified = true.
   *             ii.  Return new Success(action).
   *        d. InvalidInput:
   *             i.   Return new Failed(action, action.message).
   *   3. Return new Failed(action, "Unknown action").
   * Related Features: state, isExitSpecified, undoQuota
   * Related Classes: Action, ActionResult, Success, Failed, Move, Up, Down, Left,
   *                  Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput, GameState, Position,
   *                  StringResources
   * Input: action : Action - the action to be processed; must not be null.
   * Output: ActionResult - Success or Failed wrapping the original action and
   *         (for Failed) a human-readable reason.
   * Pre-condition: state has been initialised via setState(GameState). The
   *                caller may supply any Action produced by the input engine
   *                (including InvalidInput with initiator = -1, or actions
   *                whose initiator does not match a current player); such
   *                cases are handled by returning a Failed result.
   * Post-condition: The game state reflects the executed action. undoQuota is
   *                 decremented only when an Undo action actually consumes a
   *                 checkpoint (and never decremented by Move actions). For
   *                 Exit actions isExitSpecified is true.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public ActionResult processAction(final Action action)
  {
    if (action == null)
    {
      InvalidInput invalid = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createInvalidInput();
      invalid.setMessage("null action");
      Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
      failed.setAction(invalid);
      failed.setReason("null action");
      return failed;
    }

    if (action instanceof Move)
    {
      Move move = (Move) action;
      Position currentPos = state.getPlayerPositionById(action.getInitiator());
      Position nextPos = move.nextPosition(currentPos);
      Entity entityAtNext = state.getEntity(nextPos);
      if (entityAtNext instanceof Wall)
      {
        Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
        failed.setAction(action);
        failed.setReason("Move blocked.");
        return failed;
      }
      boolean boxPushed = entityAtNext instanceof Box;
      state.move(currentPos, nextPos);
      if (boxPushed)
      {
        state.checkpoint();
      }
      Success success = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
      success.setAction(action);
      return success;
    }
    else if (action instanceof Undo)
    {
      if (state.getUndoQuota() == 0)
      {
        Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
        failed.setAction(action);
        failed.setReason(StringResources.UNDO_QUOTA_RUN_OUT);
        return failed;
      }
      if (state.getHistory() == null || state.getHistory().isEmpty())
      {
        Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
        failed.setAction(action);
        failed.setReason("Nothing to undo.");
        return failed;
      }
      state.undo();
      if (state.getUndoQuota() != -1)
      {
        state.setUndoQuota(state.getUndoQuota() - 1);
      }
      Success success = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
      success.setAction(action);
      return success;
    }
    else if (action instanceof Exit)
    {
      setIsExitSpecified(true);
      Success success = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
      success.setAction(action);
      return success;
    }
    else if (action instanceof InvalidInput)
    {
      Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
      failed.setAction(action);
      failed.setReason(((InvalidInput) action).getMessage());
      return failed;
    }

    Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
    failed.setAction(action);
    failed.setReason("Unknown action");
    return failed;
  }

```java
        final List<String> lines = java.util.Arrays.asList(mapText.split("\\R"));
        if (lines.isEmpty() || lines.get(0).trim().isEmpty())
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid map file.");
        }
    
        final int undoLimit;
        try
        {
          undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines.get(0).trim());
        }
        catch (NumberFormatException e)
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("Failed to parse undo limit.", e);
        }
    
        if (undoLimit < -1)
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("invalid undo limit");
        }
    
        final List<String> mapLines = lines.subList(1, lines.size());
        if (mapLines.isEmpty())
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid map file.");
        }
    
        int maxHeight = mapLines.size();
        int maxWidth = 0;
        for (String line : mapLines)
        {
          if (line.length() > maxWidth)
          {
            maxWidth = line.length();
          }
        }
    
        final Map<Position, Entity> entityMap = new HashMap<Position, Entity>();
        final EList<Position> destinations = new org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList<Position>();
    
        final java.util.Set<Integer> players = new java.util.HashSet<>();
        final java.util.Set<Integer> referencedPlayers = new java.util.HashSet<>();
        int boxCount = 0;
    
        for (int y = 0; y < mapLines.size(); y++)
        {
          String line = mapLines.get(y);
          for (int x = 0; x < line.length(); x++)
          {
            char ch = line.charAt(x);
    
            Position position = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createPosition();
            position.setX(x);
            position.setY(y);
    
            switch (ch)
            {
              case '#':
                entityMap.put(position, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createWall());
                break;
              case '.':
                entityMap.put(position, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
                break;
              case '@':
                destinations.add(position);
                entityMap.put(position, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
                break;
              default:
                if (ch >= 'A' && ch <= 'Z')
                {
                  int playerId = ch - 'A';
                  if (!players.add(playerId))
                  {
                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("duplicate players detected in the map");
                  }
    
                  Player player = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlayer();
                  player.setId(playerId);
                  entityMap.put(position, player);
                }
                else if (ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z')
                {
                  int playerId = Character.toUpperCase(ch) - 'A';
                  referencedPlayers.add(playerId);
                  boxCount++;
    
                  Box box = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createBox();
                  box.setPlayerId(playerId);
                  entityMap.put(position, box);
                }
                break;
            }
          }
        }
    
        if (players.isEmpty())
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("no player");
        }
    
        if (destinations.size() != boxCount)
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("mismatch destinations");
        }
    
        if (!referencedPlayers.equals(players))
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("unmatched players");
        }
    
        GameMap gameMap = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameMap();
        gameMap.setMaxWidth(maxWidth);
        gameMap.setMaxHeight(maxHeight);
        gameMap.setUndoLimit(undoLimit);
        gameMap.getDestinations().addAll(destinations);
        gameMap.setMap(entityMap);
        return gameMap;
     
  }
```

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:

2. Algorithm: algorithm or pesudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

```text
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```
