# Operation Specifications
TerminalRenderingEngine::render
Summary:
  Renders the current GameState as ASCII art to the configured output
  stream (typically System.out), one row at a time, followed by a status
  line showing the undo quota. Each cell is drawn using the inverse of
  the map-parsing encoding: walls as '#', empty floor as '.', players as
  their upper-case letter, boxes as their lower-case letter, and a
  destination as '.'. When a box sits on a destination it is still drawn
  as the lower-case letter.
Algorithm:
  1. For y in [0, boardHeight):
       For x in [0, boardWidth):
           Entity e = state.getEntity(new Position(x, y));
           char c;
           if (e instanceof Wall)         c = '#';
           else if (e instanceof Player)  c = (char)('A' + player.id);
           else if (e instanceof Box)     c = (char)('a' + box.playerId);
           else if (state.destinations.contains(p))
                                           c = '.';
           else                            c = '.';
           outputStream.print(c);
       outputStream.println();
  2. Append a status line, e.g. "Undo quota: <state.undoQuota>", using
     StringResources.UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE.
  3. outputStream.println() to terminate the status line.
Related Features:
  - TerminalRenderingEngine.outputStream
Related Classes:
  Related Classes: GameState, EntityMap, Entity, Wall, Player, Box, Empty,
  Position, StringResources
Input:
  - state : GameState
      A non-null, initialized game state containing board dimensions,
      the entity map, the destinations list, and the undo quota.
Output:
  - void (text is written to outputStream).
Pre-condition:
  - state is non-null and internally consistent.
  - outputStream is open and writable.
Post-condition:
  - A human-readable snapshot of the game has been emitted. The
    GameState itself is not modified.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Operation Specifications
AbstractSokobanGame::processAction
Summary:
  Central action dispatcher inherited by concrete game runners (e.g.,
  TerminalSokobanGame). It mutates the internal GameState according to the
  type of Action received and returns an ActionResult (Success or Failed with
  a reason) that describes what happened.
Algorithm:
  1. If action is null, return Failed("null action").
  2. Switch on the concrete Action subclass:
     a. Move (Up/Down/Left/Right):
        - Resolve initiator player's current position from
          state.getPlayerPositionById(action.initiator).
        - Compute target via Move.nextPosition(current).
        - If target is out of board bounds, return Failed("out of bounds").
        - Get entity at target with state.getEntity(target).
        - If entity is a Wall or Player, return Failed("blocked").
        - If entity is Empty: state.move(current, target); if at least one
          entity moved (i.e., a Position was added to currentTransition),
          state.checkpoint(); return Success.
        - If entity is a Box:
            * Verify Box.getPlayerId() == action.initiator; else
              return Failed("not your box").
            * Compute beyond = move.nextPosition(target).
            * If beyond is out of bounds or state.getEntity(beyond) is not
              Empty, return Failed("cannot push").
            * Otherwise state.move(current, target) and
              state.move(target, beyond) atomically inside one transition;
              state.checkpoint() and return Success.
     b. Undo: delegate to state.undo(); if undo quota was finite and
        consumed (quota becomes -2 sentinel or quota > 0 before, 0 after,
        and a checkpoint existed), return Success; else return
        Failed("no undo available").
     c. Exit: set isExitSpecified = true; return Success.
     d. InvalidInput: return Failed with the InvalidInput.message (e.g.,
        "Invalid input").
  3. Return the produced ActionResult wrapping the action.
Related Features:
  - AbstractSokobanGame.isExitSpecified (set on Exit)
  - AbstractSokobanGame.state (mutated by moves and undos)
Related Classes:
  Related Classes: Action, ActionResult, Success, Failed, Move, Up, Down,
  Left, Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput, GameState, GameStateTransition,
  Position, Box, Empty, Wall, Player
Input:
  - action : Action
      A non-null action object produced by an InputEngine. Concrete types:
      Move (with concrete Up/Down/Left/Right), Undo, Exit, InvalidInput.
      action.initiator is an int in [0, 25] for player-initiated actions,
      -1 for InvalidInput, and unused for Exit.
Output:
  - ActionResult : either a Success wrapping the original Action, or a
    Failed carrying a human-readable reason string describing why the
    action could not be applied.
Pre-condition:
  - state is non-null and has been initialized from a valid map (at least
    one player, matching box/destination counts).
  - action is a fully constructed Action object.
Post-condition:
  - If the action was a successful Move, GameState reflects the new entity
    positions and a new transition (and possibly a checkpoint) is recorded.
  - If the action was a successful Undo, GameState is reverted to the
    previous checkpoint state and the undo quota is decreased if finite.
  - If the action was Exit, isExitSpecified is true (causing
    shouldStop() to return true).
  - In all cases an ActionResult is returned to the caller.

AbstractSokobanGame::shouldStop
Summary:
  Predicate consulted by the main game loop to determine whether the
  runner should terminate the current game. The game must stop if the user
  has explicitly issued an Exit action, or if the current board state
  already satisfies the win condition.
Algorithm:
  return isExitSpecified || state.isWin();
Related Features:
  - AbstractSokobanGame.isExitSpecified
  - AbstractSokobanGame.state
Related Classes:
  Related Classes: GameState
Input:
  - (none)
Output:
  - boolean : true if the game should terminate, false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
  - state has been initialized; isExitSpecified is a valid boolean (default
    false).
Post-condition:
  - No state mutation; the operation is side-effect free.

  2. Switch on the concrete Action subclass:
     a. Move (Up/Down/Left/Right):
        - Resolve initiator player's current position from
          state.getPlayerPositionById(action.initiator).
        - Compute target via Move.nextPosition(current).
        - If target is out of board bounds, return Failed("out of bounds").
        - Get entity at target with state.getEntity(target).
        - If entity is a Wall or Player, return Failed("blocked").
        - If entity is Empty: state.move(current, target); if at least one
          entity moved (i.e., a Position was added to currentTransition),
          state.checkpoint(); return Success.
        - If entity is a Box:
            * Verify Box.getPlayerId() == action.initiator; else
              return Failed("not your box").
            * Compute beyond = move.nextPosition(target).
            * If beyond is out of bounds or state.getEntity(beyond) is not
              Empty, return Failed("cannot push").
            * Otherwise state.move(current, target) and
              state.move(target, beyond) atomically inside one transition;
              state.checkpoint() and return Success.
     b. Undo: delegate to state.undo(); if undo quota was finite and
        consumed (quota becomes -2 sentinel or quota > 0 before, 0 after,
        and a checkpoint existed), return Success; else return
        Failed("no undo available").
     c. Exit: set isExitSpecified = true; return Success.
     d. InvalidInput: return Failed with the InvalidInput.message (e.g.,
        "Invalid input").
  3. Return the produced ActionResult wrapping the action.
Related Features:
  - AbstractSokobanGame.isExitSpecified (set on Exit)
  - AbstractSokobanGame.state (mutated by moves and undos)
Related Classes:
  Related Classes: Action, ActionResult, Success, Failed, Move, Up, Down,
  Left, Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput, GameState, GameStateTransition,
  Position, Box, Empty, Wall, Player
Input:
  - action : Action
      A non-null action object produced by an InputEngine. Concrete types:
      Move (with concrete Up/Down/Left/Right), Undo, Exit, InvalidInput.
      action.initiator is an int in [0, 25] for player-initiated actions,
      -1 for InvalidInput, and unused for Exit.
Output:
  - ActionResult : either a Success wrapping the original Action, or a
    Failed carrying a human-readable reason string describing why the
    action could not be applied.
Pre-condition:
  - state is non-null and has been initialized from a valid map (at least
    one player, matching box/destination counts).
  - action is a fully constructed Action object.
Post-condition:
  - If the action was a successful Move, GameState reflects the new entity
    positions and a new transition (and possibly a checkpoint) is recorded.
  - If the action was a successful Undo, GameState is reverted to the
    previous checkpoint state and the undo quota is decreased if finite.
  - If the action was Exit, isExitSpecified is true (causing
    shouldStop() to return true).
  - In all cases an ActionResult is returned to the caller.

AbstractSokobanGame::shouldStop
Summary:
  Predicate consulted by the main game loop to determine whether the
  runner should terminate the current game. The game must stop if the user
  has explicitly issued an Exit action, or if the current board state
  already satisfies the win condition.
Algorithm:
  return isExitSpecified || state.isWin();
Related Features:
  - AbstractSokobanGame.isExitSpecified
  - AbstractSokobanGame.state
Related Classes:
  Related Classes: GameState
Input:
  - (none)
Output:
  - boolean : true if the game should terminate, false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
  - state has been initialized; isExitSpecified is a valid boolean (default
    false).
Post-condition:
  - No state mutation; the operation is side-effect free.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

```java
  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Central action dispatcher inherited by concrete game runners (e.g.,
   *   TerminalSokobanGame). It mutates the internal GameState according to the
   *   type of Action received and returns an ActionResult (Success or Failed with
   *   a reason) that describes what happened.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If action is null, return Failed("null action").
   *   2. Switch on the concrete Action subclass:
   *      a. Move (Up/Down/Left/Right):
   *         - Resolve initiator player's current position from
   *           state.getPlayerPositionById(action.initiator).
   *         - Compute target via Move.nextPosition(current).
   *         - If target is out of board bounds, return Failed("out of bounds").
   *         - Get entity at target with state.getEntity(target).
   *         - If entity is a Wall or Player, return Failed("blocked").
   *         - If entity is Empty: state.move(current, target); return Success.
   *         - If entity is a Box:
   *             * Verify Box.getPlayerId() == action.initiator; else
   *               return Failed("not your box").
   *             * Compute beyond = move.nextPosition(target).
   *             * If beyond is out of bounds or state.getEntity(beyond) is not
   *               Empty, return Failed("cannot push").
   *             * Otherwise state.move(current, target) and
   *               state.move(target, beyond) atomically inside one transition;
   *               state.checkpoint() and return Success.
   *      b. Undo: delegate to state.undo(); if a checkpoint was successfully
   *         reverted (a checkpoint existed in history and the quota allowed
   *         it, i.e. quota was -1 unlimited or a positive finite quota),
   *         return Success; else return Failed("no undo available").
   *      c. Exit: set isExitSpecified = true; return Success.
   *      d. InvalidInput: return Failed with the InvalidInput.message (e.g.,
   *         "Invalid input").
   *   3. Return the produced ActionResult wrapping the action.
   * Related Features:
   *   - AbstractSokobanGame.isExitSpecified (set on Exit)
   *   - AbstractSokobanGame.state (mutated by moves and undos)
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: Action, ActionResult, Success, Failed, Move, Up, Down,
   *   Left, Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput, GameState, GameStateTransition,
   *   Position, Box, Empty, Wall, Player
   * Input:
   *   - action : Action
   *       A non-null action object produced by an InputEngine. Concrete types:
   *       Move (with concrete Up/Down/Left/Right), Undo, Exit, InvalidInput.
   *       action.initiator is an int in [0, 25] for player-initiated actions,
   *       -1 for InvalidInput, and unused for Exit.
   * Output:
   *   - ActionResult : either a Success wrapping the original Action, or a
   *     Failed carrying a human-readable reason string describing why the
   *     action could not be applied.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - state is non-null and has been initialized from a valid map (at least
   *     one player, matching box/destination counts).
   *   - action is a fully constructed Action object.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - If the action was a successful Empty Move, GameState reflects the new
   *     entity positions and a new transition is recorded (no checkpoint).
   *   - If the action was a successful Box-pushing Move, GameState reflects
   *     the new entity positions, a new transition is recorded, and a
   *     checkpoint is saved in the history stack.
   *   - If the action was a successful Undo, GameState is reverted to the
   *     previous checkpoint state and the undo quota is decreased if finite.
   *   - If the action was Exit, isExitSpecified is true (causing
   *     shouldStop() to return true).
   *   - In all cases an ActionResult is returned to the caller.
```

- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

```java
{
```

public ActionResult processAction(final Action action)
{
    if (action == null) {
        Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
        failed.setAction(action);
        failed.setReason("null action");
        return failed;
    }
    if (action instanceof Move) {
        Move move = (Move) action;
        Position current = getState().getPlayerPositionById(action.getInitiator());
        Position target = move.nextPosition(current);
        // Out of bounds check
        if (target.getX() < 0 || target.getX() >= getState().getBoardWidth() ||
            target.getY() < 0 || target.getY() >= getState().getBoardHeight()) {
            Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
            failed.setAction(action);
            failed.setReason("out of bounds");
            return failed;
        }
        Entity entity = getState().getEntity(target);
        if (entity instanceof Wall || entity instanceof Player) {
            Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
            failed.setAction(action);
            failed.setReason("blocked");
            return failed;
        }
        if (entity instanceof Empty) {
            getState().move(current, target);
            Success success = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
            success.setAction(action);
            return success;
        }
        if (entity instanceof Box) {
            Box box = (Box) entity;
            if (box.getPlayerId() != action.getInitiator()) {
                Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
                failed.setAction(action);
                failed.setReason("not your box");
                return failed;
            }
            Position beyond = move.nextPosition(target);
            if (beyond.getX() < 0 || beyond.getX() >= getState().getBoardWidth() ||
                beyond.getY() < 0 || beyond.getY() >= getState().getBoardHeight() ||
                !(getState().getEntity(beyond) instanceof Empty)) {
                Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
                failed.setAction(action);
                failed.setReason("cannot push");
                return failed;
            }
            getState().move(current, target);
            getState().move(target, beyond);
            getState().checkpoint();
            Success success = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
            success.setAction(action);
            return success;
        }
    } else if (action instanceof Undo) {
        // Need to determine if undo was successful
        int beforeQuota = getState().getUndoQuota();
        int beforeHistorySize = getState().getHistory().size();
        getState().undo();
        // After undo: if quota was -1 (unlimited), still success. If quota > 0 before, it decreases. 
        // If history was empty or quota was 0, undo did nothing
        boolean success = (beforeHistorySize > 0) && (beforeQuota == -1 || beforeQuota > 0);
        if (success) {
            Success s = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
            s.setAction(action);
            return s;
        } else {
            Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
            failed.setAction(action);
            failed.setReason("no undo available");
            return failed;
        }
    } else if (action instanceof Exit) {
        setIsExitSpecified(true);
        Success success = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
        success.setAction(action);
        return success;
    } else if (action instanceof InvalidInput) {
        InvalidInput invalid = (InvalidInput) action;
        Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
        failed.setAction(action);
        failed.setReason(invalid.getMessage() != null ? invalid.getMessage() : "Invalid input");
        return failed;
    }
    // Default - shouldn't happen, but safe fallback
    Failed failed = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
    failed.setAction(action);
    failed.setReason("unknown action");
    return failed;
}

5. Do not change other part.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

```java
package edu.pa22;

import java.util.Collection;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeSet;

import org.eclipse.emf.common.notify.Notification;

import org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList;
import org.eclipse.emf.common.util.EList;

import org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EClass;
import org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EObject;

import org.eclipse.emf.ecore.impl.ENotificationImpl;
import org.eclipse.emf.ecore.impl.MinimalEObjectImpl;

import org.eclipse.emf.ecore.util.EObjectResolvingEList;

public class GameMap extends MinimalEObjectImpl.Container implements EObject
{
  // ... existing fields and methods ...
  
  public EList<Integer> getPlayerIds()
  {
    TreeSet<Integer> ids = new TreeSet<Integer>();
    Map<Position, Entity> entityMap = getMap();
    if (entityMap != null)
    {
      for (Entity entity : entityMap.values())
      {
        if (entity instanceof Player)
        {
          ids.add(Integer.valueOf(((Player) entity).getId()));
        }
      }
    }
    return new BasicEList<Integer>(ids);
  }
  
  public void putEntity(final Position position, final Entity entity)
  {
    getMap().put(position, entity);
  }
}
```

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
```java
   *   Atomically relocates whatever Entity currently sits at `from` to `to`,
   *   leaving the source cell as Empty, and records the move inside the
   *   current GameStateTransition so it can be undone later. This is the
   *   primitive used both for a player walking and for a player pushing a
   *   box (the push issues two moves: player and box).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Look up entity = entities.getEntity(from). It must not be Empty/Wall.
   *   2. If entities.getEntity(to) is not Empty and not the same entity being
   *      moved (used during push: the box), the move is invalid; abort.
   *   3. entities.putEntity(from, new Empty());
   *      entities.putEntity(to, entity);
   *   4. currentTransition.add(from, to);   // record the swap
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.entities
   *   - GameState.currentTransition
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: EntityMap, Entity, Empty, Box, Player, Position,
   *   GameStateTransition
   * Input:
   *   - from : Position
   *       The source cell currently containing the entity to move. Must be
   *       non-null and within bounds, and must contain a movable entity
   *       (Player or Box).
   *   - to   : Position
   *       The destination cell. Must be non-null, within bounds, and either
   *       Empty or - in the case of pushing a box - already logically emptied
   *       by the calling code.
   * Output:
   *   - void
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - from and to are valid in-bounds positions.
   *   - from contains a movable entity (Player or Box).
   *   - to is Empty (for a player move) or will be the trailing cell beyond a
   *     box that is also being moved in the same transition.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - entities reflects the move: from is Empty, to holds the relocated
   *     entity.
   *   - currentTransition.moves records (from -> to) so undo() can revert it.

   * Summary:

   *   box is successfully pushed (the caller, e.g. processAction, invokes

   *   }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Reverts the game state to the most recent checkpoint by popping the
   *   top GameStateTransition off the history stack and applying its
   *   reverse() atomically. A finite undo quota is decremented only when a
   *   checkpoint was actually consumed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If undoQuota == 0, do nothing (undo is not allowed when quota is 0).
   *   2. If history is empty, do nothing (quota is not consumed).
   *   3. GameStateTransition last = history.pop();
   *   4. GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
   *   5. For each (to, from) in reversed.moves:
   *        entities.putEntity(to, new Empty());
   *        entities.putEntity(from, entityRecordedInReversedMove);
   *   6. currentTransition = new GameStateTransition();
   *   7. If undoQuota == -1 (unlimited), keep it; else if undoQuota > 0,
   *      decrement by 1.
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.history
   *   - GameState.currentTransition (reset to empty)
   *   - GameState.undoQuota
   *   - GameState.entities (mutated to reflect the undo)
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: GameStateTransition, TransitionStack, EntityMap, Empty
   * Input:
   *   - (none)
   * Output:
   *   - void
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - undoQuota != 0 (the caller guards against invoking undo() when the
   *     quota is exhausted).
   *   - history contains at least one checkpoint transition, otherwise undo()
   *     is a no-op and the quota is not consumed.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - All entity positions recorded in the popped transition are restored
   *     to their pre-move locations.
   *   - undoQuota is decremented by 1 if it was a positive finite value;
   *     unchanged if it was -1 (unlimited).
   *   - currentTransition is replaced with a fresh empty transition.

   * Algorithm:
```

```java
   *   6. currentTransition = new GameStateTransition();

   * Summary:
```
```java
   *   Reverts the game state to the most recent checkpoint by popping the
   *   top GameStateTransition off the history stack and applying its
   *   reverse() atomically. A finite undo quota is decremented only when a
   *   checkpoint was actually consumed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If undoQuota == 0, do nothing (undo is not allowed when quota is 0).
   *   2. If history is empty, do nothing (quota is not consumed).
   *   3. GameStateTransition last = history.pop();
   *   4. GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
   *   5. For each (to, from) in reversed.moves:
   *        entities.putEntity(to, new Empty());
   *        entities.putEntity(from, entityRecordedInReversedMove);
   *   6. currentTransition = new GameStateTransition();
   *   7. If undoQuota == -1 (unlimited), keep it; else if undoQuota > 0,
   *      decrement by 1.
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.history
   *   - GameState.currentTransition (reset to empty)
   *   - GameState.undoQuota

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
```
```java
   *   Atomically relocates whatever Entity currently sits at `from` to `to`,
   *   leaving the source cell as Empty, and records the move inside the
   *   current GameStateTransition so it can be undone later. This is the
   *   primitive used both for a player walking and for a player pushing a
   *   box (the push issues two moves: player and box).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Look up entity = entities.getEntity(from). It must not be Empty/Wall.
   *   2. If entities.getEntity(to) is not Empty and not the same entity being
   *      moved (used during push: the box), the move is invalid; abort.
   *   3. entities.putEntity(from, new Empty());
   *      entities.putEntity(to, entity);
   *   4. currentTransition.add(from, to);   // record the swap
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.entities
   *   - GameState.currentTransition
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: EntityMap, Entity, Empty, Box, Player, Position,
   *   GameStateTransition
   * Input:
   *   - from : Position
   *       The source cell currently containing the entity to move. Must be
   *       non-null and within bounds, and must contain a movable entity
   *       (Player or Box).
   *   - to   : Position
   *       The destination cell. Must be non-null, within bounds, and either
   *       Empty or - in the case of pushing a box - already logically emptied
   *       by the calling code.
   * Output:
   *   - void
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - from and to are valid in-bounds positions.
   *   - from contains a movable entity (Player or Box).
   *   - to is Empty (for a player move) or will be the trailing cell beyond a
   *     box that is also being moved in the same transition.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - entities reflects the move: from is Empty, to holds the relocated
   *     entity.
   *   - currentTransition.moves records (from -> to) so undo() can revert it.

   * Summary:

   *   can be reverted to later by undo(). A checkpoint is recorded when a
   *   box is successfully pushed (the caller, e.g. processAction, invokes

   *   }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Reverts the game state to the most recent checkpoint by popping the
   *   top GameStateTransition off the history stack and applying its
   *   reverse() atomically. A finite undo quota is decremented only when a
   *   checkpoint was actually consumed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If undoQuota == 0, do nothing (undo is not allowed when quota is 0).
   *   2. If history is empty, do nothing (quota is not consumed).
   *   3. GameStateTransition last = history.pop();
   *   4. GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
   *   5. For each (to, from) in reversed.moves:
   *        entities.putEntity(to, new Empty());
   *        entities.putEntity(from, entityRecordedInReversedMove);
   *   6. currentTransition = new GameStateTransition();
   *   7. If undoQuota == -1 (unlimited), keep it; else if undoQuota > 0,
   *      decrement by 1.
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.history
   *   - GameState.currentTransition (reset to empty)
   *   - GameState.undoQuota
   *   - GameState.entities (mutated to reflect the undo)
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: GameStateTransition, TransitionStack, EntityMap, Empty
   * Input:
   *   - (none)
   * Output:
   *   - void
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - undoQuota != 0 (the caller guards against invoking undo() when the
   *     quota is exhausted).
   *   - history contains at least one checkpoint transition, otherwise undo()
   *     is a no-op and the quota is not consumed.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - All entity positions recorded in the popped transition are restored
   *     to their pre-move locations.
   *   - undoQuota is decremented by 1 if it was a positive finite value;
   *     unchanged if it was -1 (unlimited).
   *   - currentTransition is replaced with a fresh empty transition.

   * Summary:

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
```
```java
   *   Reverts the game state to the most recent checkpoint by popping the
   *   top GameStateTransition off the history stack and applying its
   *   reverse() atomically. A finite undo quota is decremented only when a
   *   checkpoint was actually consumed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If undoQuota == 0, do nothing (undo is not allowed when quota is 0).
   *   2. If history is empty, do nothing (quota is not consumed).
   *   3. GameStateTransition last = history.pop();
   *   4. GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
   *   5. For each (to, from) in reversed.moves:
   *        entities.putEntity(to, new Empty());
   *        entities.putEntity(from, entityRecordedInReversedMove);
   *   6. currentTransition = new GameStateTransition();
   *   7. If undoQuota == -1 (unlimited), keep it; else if undoQuota > 0,
   *      decrement by 1.
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.history
   *   - GameState.currentTransition (reset to empty)
   *   - GameState.undoQuota
   *   - GameState.entities (mutated to reflect the undo)
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: GameStateTransition, TransitionStack, EntityMap, Empty
   * Input:
   *   - (none)
   * Output:
   *   - void
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - undoQuota != 0 (the caller guards against invoking undo() when the
   *     quota is exhausted).
   *   - history contains at least one checkpoint transition, otherwise undo()
   *     is a no-op and the quota is not consumed.
   * Post-condition:

   *     to their pre-move locations.
   *   - undoQuota is decremented by 1 if it was a positive finite value;

  /**

   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
```
```java
   *   Reverts the game state to the most recent checkpoint by popping the
   *   top GameStateTransition off the history stack and applying its
   *   reverse() atomically. A finite undo quota is decremented only when a
   *   checkpoint was actually consumed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If undoQuota == 0, do nothing (undo is not allowed when quota is 0).
   *   2. If history is empty, do nothing (quota is not consumed).
   *   3. GameStateTransition last = history.pop();
   *   4. GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
   *   5. For each (to, from) in reversed.moves:
   *        entities.putEntity(to, new Empty());
   *        entities.putEntity(from, entityRecordedInReversedMove);
   *   6. currentTransition = new GameStateTransition();
   *   7. If undoQuota == -1 (unlimited), keep it; else if undoQuota > 0,
   *      decrement by 1.
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.history
   *   - GameState.currentTransition (reset to empty)

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
```
```java
   *   Atomically relocates whatever Entity currently sits at `from` to `to`,
   *   leaving the source cell as Empty, and records the move inside the
   *   current GameStateTransition so it can be undone later. This is the
   *   primitive used both for a player walking and for a player pushing a
   *   box (the push issues two moves: player and box).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Look up entity = entities.getEntity(from). It must not be Empty/Wall.
   *   2. If entities.getEntity(to) is not Empty and not the same entity being
   *      moved (used during push: the box), the move is invalid; abort.
   *   3. entities.putEntity(from, new Empty());
   *      entities.putEntity(to, entity);
   *   4. currentTransition.add(from, to);   // record the swap
   * Related Features:

   *       (Player or Box).
   *   - to   : Position

   *       Empty or - in the case of pushing a box - already logically emptied
   *       by the calling code.

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Reverts the game state to the most recent checkpoint by popping the
   *   top GameStateTransition off the history stack and applying its
   *   reverse() atomically. A finite undo quota is decremented only when a
   *   checkpoint was actually consumed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If undoQuota == 0, do nothing (undo is not allowed when quota is 0).
   *   2. If history is empty, do nothing (quota is not consumed).
   *   3. GameStateTransition last = history.pop();
   *   4. GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
   *   5. For each (to, from) in reversed.moves:
   *        entities.putEntity(to, new Empty());
   *        entities.putEntity(from, entityRecordedInReversedMove);
   *   6. currentTransition = new GameStateTransition();
   *   7. If undoQuota == -1 (unlimited), keep it; else if undoQuota > 0,
   *      decrement by 1.
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.history
   *   - GameState.currentTransition (reset to empty)
   *   - GameState.undoQuota
   *   - GameState.entities (mutated to reflect the undo)
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: GameStateTransition, TransitionStack, EntityMap, Empty
   * Input:
   *   - (none)
   * Output:
   *   - void
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - undoQuota != 0 (the caller guards against invoking undo() when the
   *     quota is exhausted).
   *   - history contains at least one checkpoint transition, otherwise undo()
   *     is a no-op and the quota is not consumed.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - All entity positions recorded in the popped transition are restored
   *     to their pre-move locations.
   *   - undoQuota is decremented by 1 if it was a positive finite value;
   *     unchanged if it was -1 (unlimited).
```

```java
public void move(final Position from, final Position to)
{
```
```java
  Entity entity = getEntities().get(from);
  if (entity instanceof Empty || entity instanceof Wall) {
    return;  // invalid
  }
  Entity destEntity = getEntities().get(to);
  if (!(destEntity instanceof Empty) && destEntity != entity) {
    return;  // invalid
  }
  getEntities().put(from, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
  getEntities().put(to, entity);
  if (getCurrentTransition() != null) {
    getCurrentTransition().add(from, to);
  }
}
```

**`undo()`**:
```java
public void undo()
{
  if (getUndoQuota() == 0) return;
  if (getHistory().isEmpty()) return;
  GameStateTransition last = getHistory().pop();
  GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
  for (Entry<Position, Position> e : reversed.getMoves().entrySet()) {
    Position to = e.getKey();
    Position from = e.getValue();
    Entity entity = getEntities().get(to);
    getEntities().put(to, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
    getEntities().put(from, entity);
  }
  setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
  if (getUndoQuota() > 0) {
    setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);
  }
}
```

```java
public boolean isWin()
{
  for (Position dest : getDestinations()) {
    Entity e = getEntities().get(dest);
    if (!(e instanceof Box)) {
      return false;
    }
  }
  return true;
}
```

```java
public Position getPlayerPositionById(final int id)
```

**`getAllPlayerPositions()`**:
```java
public EList<Position> getAllPlayerPositions()
{
  List<Entry<Integer, Position>> players = new ArrayList<Entry<Integer, Position>>();
  for (Entry<Position, Entity> e : getEntities().entrySet()) {
    Entity ent = e.getValue();
    if (ent instanceof Player) {
      players.add(new java.util.AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<Integer, Position>(((Player) ent).getId(), e.getKey()));
    }
  }
  players.sort(new Comparator<Entry<Integer, Position>>() {
    public int compare(Entry<Integer, Position> a, Entry<Integer, Position> b) {
      return Integer.compare(a.getKey(), b.getKey());
    }
  });
  EList<Position> result = new BasicEList<Position>();
  for (Entry<Integer, Position> p : players) {
    result.add(p.getValue());
  }
  return result;
}
```

**`undo()`**:
```java
public void undo()
{
  if (getUndoQuota() == 0) return;
  if (getHistory().isEmpty()) return;
  GameStateTransition last = getHistory().pop();
  GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
  for (Entry<Position, Position> e : reversed.getMoves().entrySet()) {
    Position to = e.getKey();
    Position from = e.getValue();
    Entity entity = getEntities().get(to);
    getEntities().put(to, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
    getEntities().put(from, entity);
  }
  setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
  if (getUndoQuota() > 0) {
    setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);
  }
}
```

```java
public EList<Position> getAllPlayerPositions()
{
  List<Entry<Integer, Position>> players = new ArrayList<Entry<Integer, Position>>();
  for (Entry<Position, Entity> e : getEntities().entrySet()) {
    Entity ent = e.getValue();
    if (ent instanceof Player) {
      players.add(new java.util.AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<Integer, Position>(((Player) ent).getId(), e.getKey()));
    }
  }
  players.sort(new Comparator<Entry<Integer, Position>>() {
    public int compare(Entry<Integer, Position> a, Entry<Integer, Position> b) {
      return Integer.compare(a.getKey(), b.getKey());
    }
  });
  EList<Position> result = new BasicEList<Position>();
  for (Entry<Integer, Position> p : players) {
    result.add(p.getValue());
  }
  return result;
}
```

For `undo()`:
```java
public void undo()
{
  if (getUndoQuota() == 0) {
    return;
  }
  if (getHistory().isEmpty()) {
    return;
  }
  GameStateTransition last = getHistory().pop();
  GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
  for (Entry<Position, Position> entry : reversed.getMoves().entrySet()) {
    Position to = entry.getKey();
    Position from = entry.getValue();
    Entity entity = getEntities().get(to);
    getEntities().put(to, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
    getEntities().put(from, entity);
  }
  setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
  if (getUndoQuota() > 0) {
    setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);
  }
}
```

```java
public EList<Position> getAllPlayerPositions()
{
  List<Entry<Integer, Position>> players = new ArrayList<Entry<Integer, Position>>();
  for (Entry<Position, Entity> entry : getEntities().entrySet()) {
    Entity ent = entry.getValue();
    if (ent instanceof Player) {
      players.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<Integer, Position>(((Player) ent).getId(), entry.getKey()));
    }
  }
  players.sort(new Comparator<Entry<Integer, Position>>() {
    public int compare(Entry<Integer, Position> a, Entry<Integer, Position> b) {
      return Integer.compare(a.getKey(), b.getKey());
    }
  });
  EList<Position> result = new BasicEList<Position>();
  for (Entry<Integer, Position> p : players) {
    result.add(p.getValue());
  }
  return result;
}
```

```java
public void move(final Position from, final Position to)
```

```java
public void move(final Position from, final Position to)
{
```
```java
  Entity entity = getEntities().get(from);
  if (entity instanceof Empty || entity instanceof Wall) {
    return;  // invalid
  }
  Entity destEntity = getEntities().get(to);
  if (!(destEntity instanceof Empty) && destEntity != entity) {
    return;  // invalid
  }
  getEntities().put(from, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
  getEntities().put(to, entity);
  if (getCurrentTransition() != null) {
    getCurrentTransition().add(from, to);
  }
}
```

```java
    setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
  }
}
```

**`undo()`**:
```java
public void undo()
{
  if (getUndoQuota() == 0) return;
  if (getHistory().isEmpty()) return;
  GameStateTransition last = getHistory().pop();
  GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
  for (Entry<Position, Position> e : reversed.getMoves().entrySet()) {
    Position to = e.getKey();
    Position from = e.getValue();
    Entity entity = getEntities().get(to);
    getEntities().put(to, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
    getEntities().put(from, entity);
  }
  setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
  if (getUndoQuota() > 0) {
    setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);
  }
}
```

**`isWin()`**:
```java
public boolean isWin()
{
  for (Position dest : getDestinations()) {
    Entity e = getEntities().get(dest);
    if (!(e instanceof Box)) {
      return false;
    }
  }
  return true;
}
```

```java
public Position getPlayerPositionById(final int id)

      return e.getKey();
    }
  }

}
```

```java
public EList<Position> getAllPlayerPositions()
{
  List<Entry<Integer, Position>> players = new ArrayList<Entry<Integer, Position>>();
  for (Entry<Position, Entity> e : getEntities().entrySet()) {
    Entity ent = e.getValue();
    if (ent instanceof Player) {
      players.add(new java.util.AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<Integer, Position>(((Player) ent).getId(), e.getKey()));
    }
  }
  players.sort(new Comparator<Entry<Integer, Position>>() {
    public int compare(Entry<Integer, Position> a, Entry<Integer, Position> b) {
      return Integer.compare(a.getKey(), b.getKey());
    }
  });
  EList<Position> result = new BasicEList<Position>();
  for (Entry<Integer, Position> p : players) {
    result.add(p.getValue());
  }
  return result;
}
```

For `undo()`:
```java
public void undo()
{
  if (getUndoQuota() == 0) {
    return;
  }
  if (getHistory().isEmpty()) {
    return;
  }
  GameStateTransition last = getHistory().pop();
  GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
  for (Entry<Position, Position> entry : reversed.getMoves().entrySet()) {
    Position to = entry.getKey();
    Position from = entry.getValue();
    Entity entity = getEntities().get(to);
    getEntities().put(to, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
    getEntities().put(from, entity);
  }
  setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
  if (getUndoQuota() > 0) {
    setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);
  }
}
```

```java
public void move(final Position from, final Position to)
```

```java
public EList<Position> getAllPlayerPositions()
{
  List<Map.Entry<Integer, Position>> players = new ArrayList<Map.Entry<Integer, Position>>();
  for (Map.Entry<Position, Entity> entry : getEntities().entrySet())
  {
    Entity ent = entry.getValue();
    if (ent instanceof Player)
    {
      players.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<Integer, Position>(((Player) ent).getId(), entry.getKey()));
    }
  }
  java.util.Collections.sort(players, new Comparator<Map.Entry<Integer, Position>>()
  {
    public int compare(Map.Entry<Integer, Position> a, Map.Entry<Integer, Position> b)
    {
      return Integer.compare(a.getKey(), b.getKey());
    }
  });
  EList<Position> result = new BasicEList<Position>();
  for (Map.Entry<Integer, Position> p : players)
  {
    result.add(p.getValue());
  }
  return result;
}
```

```java
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Atomically relocates whatever Entity currently sits at `from` to `to`,
   *   leaving the source cell as Empty, and records the move inside the
   *   current GameStateTransition so it can be undone later. This is the
   *   primitive used both for a player walking and for a player pushing a
   *   box (the push issues two moves: player and box).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Look up entity = entities.getEntity(from). It must not be Empty/Wall.
   *   2. If entities.getEntity(to) is not Empty and not the same entity being
   *      moved (used during push: the box), the move is invalid; abort.
   *   3. entities.putEntity(from, new Empty());
   *      entities.putEntity(to, entity);
   *   4. currentTransition.add(from, to);   // record the swap
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.entities
   *   - GameState.currentTransition
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: EntityMap, Entity, Empty, Box, Player, Position,
   *   GameStateTransition
   * Input:
   *   - from : Position
   *       The source cell currently containing the entity to move. Must be
   *       non-null and within bounds, and must contain a movable entity
   *       (Player or Box).
   *   - to   : Position
   *       The destination cell. Must be non-null, within bounds, and either
   *       Empty or - in the case of pushing a box - already logically emptied
   *       by the calling code.
   * Output:
   *   - void
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - from and to are valid in-bounds positions.
   *   - from contains a movable entity (Player or Box).
   *   - to is Empty (for a player move) or will be the trailing cell beyond a
   *     box that is also being moved in the same transition.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - entities reflects the move: from is Empty, to holds the relocated
   *     entity.
   *   - currentTransition.moves records (from -> to) so undo() can revert it.

   * Summary:

   *   box is successfully pushed (the caller, e.g. processAction, invokes

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Reverts the game state to the most recent checkpoint by popping the
   *   top GameStateTransition off the history stack and applying its
   *   reverse() atomically. A finite undo quota is decremented only when a
   *   checkpoint was actually consumed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If undoQuota == 0, do nothing (undo is not allowed when quota is 0).
   *   2. If history is empty, do nothing (quota is not consumed).
   *   3. GameStateTransition last = history.pop();
   *   4. GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
   *   5. For each (to, from) in reversed.moves:
   *        entities.putEntity(to, new Empty());
   *        entities.putEntity(from, entityRecordedInReversedMove);
   *   6. currentTransition = new GameStateTransition();
   *   7. If undoQuota == -1 (unlimited), keep it; else if undoQuota > 0,
   *      decrement by 1.
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.history
   *   - GameState.currentTransition (reset to empty)
   *   - GameState.undoQuota
   *   - GameState.entities (mutated to reflect the undo)
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: GameStateTransition, TransitionStack, EntityMap, Empty
   * Input:
   *   - (none)
   * Output:
   *   - void
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - undoQuota != 0 (the caller guards against invoking undo() when the
   *     quota is exhausted).
   *   - history contains at least one checkpoint transition, otherwise undo()
   *     is a no-op and the quota is not consumed.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - All entity positions recorded in the popped transition are restored
   *     to their pre-move locations.
   *   - undoQuota is decremented by 1 if it was a positive finite value;
   *     unchanged if it was -1 (unlimited).
   *   - currentTransition is replaced with a fresh empty transition.
```

```java
  if (entity instanceof Empty || entity instanceof Wall) {
    return;  // invalid
  }

}
```

**`undo()`**:
```java
public void undo()
{
  if (getUndoQuota() == 0) return;
  if (getHistory().isEmpty()) return;
  GameStateTransition last = getHistory().pop();
  GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
  for (Entry<Position, Position> e : reversed.getMoves().entrySet()) {
    Position to = e.getKey();
    Position from = e.getValue();
    Entity entity = getEntities().get(to);
    getEntities().put(to, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
    getEntities().put(from, entity);
  }
  setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
  if (getUndoQuota() > 0) {
    setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);
  }
}
```

**`getAllPlayerPositions()`**:
```java
public EList<Position> getAllPlayerPositions()
{
  List<Entry<Integer, Position>> players = new ArrayList<Entry<Integer, Position>>();
  for (Entry<Position, Entity> e : getEntities().entrySet()) {
    Entity ent = e.getValue();
    if (ent instanceof Player) {
      players.add(new java.util.AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<Integer, Position>(((Player) ent).getId(), e.getKey()));
    }
  }
  players.sort(new Comparator<Entry<Integer, Position>>() {
    public int compare(Entry<Integer, Position> a, Entry<Integer, Position> b) {
      return Integer.compare(a.getKey(), b.getKey());
    }
  });
  EList<Position> result = new BasicEList<Position>();
  for (Entry<Integer, Position> p : players) {
    result.add(p.getValue());
  }
  return result;
}
```

For `undo()`:
```java
public void undo()
{
  if (getUndoQuota() == 0) {
    return;
  }
  if (getHistory().isEmpty()) {
    return;
  }
  GameStateTransition last = getHistory().pop();
  GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
  for (Entry<Position, Position> entry : reversed.getMoves().entrySet()) {
    Position to = entry.getKey();
    Position from = entry.getValue();
    Entity entity = getEntities().get(to);
    getEntities().put(to, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
    getEntities().put(from, entity);
  }
  setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
  if (getUndoQuota() > 0) {
    setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);
  }
}
```

```java
public EList<Position> getAllPlayerPositions()
{
  List<Entry<Integer, Position>> players = new ArrayList<Entry<Integer, Position>>();
  for (Entry<Position, Entity> entry : getEntities().entrySet()) {
    Entity ent = entry.getValue();
    if (ent instanceof Player) {
      players.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<Integer, Position>(((Player) ent).getId(), entry.getKey()));
    }
  }
  players.sort(new Comparator<Entry<Integer, Position>>() {
    public int compare(Entry<Integer, Position> a, Entry<Integer, Position> b) {
      return Integer.compare(a.getKey(), b.getKey());
    }
  });
  EList<Position> result = new BasicEList<Position>();
  for (Entry<Integer, Position> p : players) {
    result.add(p.getValue());
  }
  return result;
}
```

```java
   * Summary:
```
```java
   *   Atomically relocates whatever Entity currently sits at `from` to `to`,
   *   leaving the source cell as Empty, and records the move inside the
   *   current GameStateTransition so it can be undone later. This is the
   *   primitive used both for a player walking and for a player pushing a
   *   box (the push issues two moves: player and box).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Look up entity = entities.getEntity(from). It must not be Empty/Wall.
   *   2. If entities.getEntity(to) is not Empty and not the same entity being
   *      moved (used during push: the box), the move is invalid; abort.
   *   3. entities.putEntity(from, new Empty());
   *      entities.putEntity(to, entity);
   *   4. currentTransition.add(from, to);   // record the swap
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.entities
   *   - GameState.currentTransition
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: EntityMap, Entity, Empty, Box, Player, Position,
   *   GameStateTransition
   * Input:
   *   - from : Position
   *       The source cell currently containing the entity to move. Must be
   *       non-null and within bounds, and must contain a movable entity
   *       (Player or Box).
   *   - to   : Position
   *       The destination cell. Must be non-null, within bounds, and either
   *       Empty or - in the case of pushing a box - already logically emptied
   *       by the calling code.
   * Output:

   * Pre-condition:
   *   - from and to are valid in-bounds positions.
   *   - from contains a movable entity (Player or Box).
   *   - to is Empty (for a player move) or will be the trailing cell beyond a
   *     box that is also being moved in the same transition.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - entities reflects the move: from is Empty, to holds the relocated
   *     entity.
   *   - currentTransition.moves records (from -> to) so undo() can revert it.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void move(final Position from, final Position to)
  {
    Entity entity = getEntities().get(from);
    if (entity instanceof Empty || entity instanceof Wall)
    {
      return;
    }
    Entity destEntity = getEntities().get(to);
    if (!(destEntity instanceof Empty) && destEntity != entity)
    {
      return;
    }
    getEntities().put(from, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
    getEntities().put(to, entity);
    if (getCurrentTransition() != null)
    {
      getCurrentTransition().add(from, to);
    }
  }

   *   Snapshots the current GameStateTransition onto the history stack so it
   *   can be reverted to later by undo(). A checkpoint is recorded when a
   *   box is successfully pushed (the caller, e.g. processAction, invokes

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Reverts the game state to the most recent checkpoint by popping the
   *   top GameStateTransition off the history stack and applying its
   *   reverse() atomically. A finite undo quota is decremented only when a
   *   checkpoint was actually consumed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If undoQuota == 0, do nothing (undo is not allowed when quota is 0).
   *   2. If history is empty, do nothing (quota is not consumed).
   *   3. GameStateTransition last = history.pop();
   *   4. GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
   *   5. For each (to, from) in reversed.moves:
   *        entities.putEntity(to, new Empty());
   *        entities.putEntity(from, entityRecordedInReversedMove);
   *   6. currentTransition = new GameStateTransition();
   *   7. If undoQuota == -1 (unlimited), keep it; else if undoQuota > 0,
   *      decrement by 1.
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.history
   *   - GameState.currentTransition (reset to empty)
   *   - GameState.undoQuota
   *   - GameState.entities (mutated to reflect the undo)
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: GameStateTransition, TransitionStack, EntityMap, Empty
   * Input:
   *   - (none)
   * Output:
   *   - void
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - undoQuota != 0 (the caller guards against invoking undo() when the
   *     quota is exhausted).
   *   - history contains at least one checkpoint transition, otherwise undo() 
   *     is a no-op and the quota is not consumed.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - All entity positions recorded in the popped transition are restored
   *     to their pre-move locations.
   *   - undoQuota is decremented by 1 if it was a positive finite value;
   *     unchanged if it was -1 (unlimited).
   *   - currentTransition is replaced with a fresh empty transition.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void undo()
  {
    if (getUndoQuota() == 0)
    {
      return;
    }
    if (getHistory().isEmpty())
    {
      return;
    }
    GameStateTransition last = getHistory().pop();
    GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
    for (Map.Entry<Position, Position> entry : reversed.getMoves().entrySet())
    {
      Position toPos = entry.getKey();
      Position fromPos = entry.getValue();
      Entity entity = getEntities().get(toPos);
      getEntities().put(toPos, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
      getEntities().put(fromPos, entity);
    }
    setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
    if (getUndoQuota() > 0)
    {
      setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);
    }
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Returns the current grid positions of every Player on the board, in
   *   ascending order of player ID.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Iterate over entities.
   *   2. For each cell, if the entity is a Player, record its Position
   *      together with the player's id.
   *   3. Sort the collected entries by player id (ascending) and return the
   *      Positions in that order.
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.entities (source of player locations)
   * Related Classes:
   *   Related Classes: Position, Player
   * Input:
   *   - (none)
   * Output:
   *   - List<Position> : one Position per active player, in ascending player
   *     ID order. Empty if the game has no players (which should not occur in
   *     a valid game).
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - The state has been initialized from a valid map containing at least
   *     one player.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - The returned list is a fresh snapshot; GameState is not modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model kind="operation"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public EList<Position> getAllPlayerPositions()
  {
    List<Map.Entry<Integer, Position>> players = new ArrayList<Map.Entry<Integer, Position>>();
    for (Map.Entry<Position, Entity> entry : getEntities().entrySet())
    {
      Entity ent = entry.getValue();
      if (ent instanceof Player)
      {
        players.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<Integer, Position>(((Player) ent).getId(), entry.getKey()));
      }
    }
    players.sort(new Comparator<Map.Entry<Integer, Position>>()
    {
      public int compare(Map.Entry<Integer, Position> a, Map.Entry<Integer, Position> b)
      {
        return Integer.compare(a.getKey(), b.getKey());
      }
    });
    EList<Position> result = new BasicEList<Position>();
    for (Map.Entry<Integer, Position> p : players)
    {
      result.add(p.getValue());
    }
    return result;
  }

  /**
```

Now, one more thought: the entity at `toPos` should be the entity that was recorded in the (original) move. But the entity is captured at the current state, not from the transition. So this only works correctly if the state hasn't been modified since the move was recorded.

In a normal undo flow:
1. Move: state updated, transition recorded.
2. Maybe more moves.
3. Checkpoint: transition pushed to history.
4. Undo: pop transition, reverse, apply reverse to state.

Between step 1 and step 4, the state may have been modified by subsequent moves. So when we undo, the entity at `toPos` (in the reversed map) might not be the same as what was originally moved there.

For example:
- Original move: move(player, A, A+1). State: A=empty, A+1=player. Transition: {A -> A+1}.
- Subsequent move: move(player, A+1, A+2). State: A+1=empty, A+2=player. Transition: {A -> A+1, A+1 -> A+2}.
- Checkpoint. History has {A -> A+1, A+1 -> A+2}.
- Undo. Pop, reverse: {(A+2, A+1), (A+1, A)} where key=to, value=from. So entries are: (A+2, A+1) and (A+1, A).
  - Process (A+2, A+1): entity at A+2 is player. Put empty at A+2, put player at A+1. State: A=empty, A+1=player, A+2=empty.
  - Process (A+1, A): entity at A+1 is player. Put empty at A+1, put player at A. State: A=player, A+1=empty, A+2=empty. ✓

OK this works because we process in order. The iteration order of the reversed map matters.

If the original transition was {A -> A+1, A+1 -> A+2}, the reversed would be... well, it depends on the `reverse()` implementation. If `reverse()` just iterates the original and adds entries in the same order, the reversed map has keys {A+1, A+2}. Iterating gives A+1, A+2 (or A+2, A+1 depending on Map type).

If the iteration is in insertion order (LinkedHashMap-like):
- Iter 1: (A+1, A). Entity at A+1 is player. Put empty at A+1, put player at A. State: A=player, A+1=empty, A+2=player. Then iter 2: (A+2, A+1). Entity at A+2 is player. Put empty at A+2, put player at A+1. State: A=player, A+1=player, A+2=empty. ✗ WRONG.

If the iteration is in reverse insertion order:
- Iter 1: (A+2, A+1). Entity at A+2 is player. Put empty at A+2, put player at A+1. State: A=empty, A+1=player, A+2=empty. Then iter 2: (A+1, A). Entity at A+1 is player. Put empty at A+1, put player at A. State: A=player, A+1=empty, A+2=empty. ✓ CORRECT.

```java
public EList<Position> getAllPlayerPositions()
{
  List<Map.Entry<Integer, Position>> players = new ArrayList<Map.Entry<Integer, Position>>();
  for (Map.Entry<Position, Entity> entry : getEntities().entrySet())
  {
    Entity ent = entry.getValue();
    if (ent instanceof Player)
    {
      players.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<Integer, Position>(((Player) ent).getId(), entry.getKey()));
    }
  }
  players.sort(new Comparator<Map.Entry<Integer, Position>>()
  {
    public int compare(Map.Entry<Integer, Position> a, Map.Entry<Integer, Position> b)
    {
      return Integer.compare(a.getKey(), b.getKey());
    }
  });
  EList<Position> result = new BasicEList<Position>();
  for (Map.Entry<Integer, Position> p : players)
  {
    result.add(p.getValue());
  }
  return result;
}
```

This uses `List.sort(Comparator)` (Java 8+) and `Integer.compare(int, int)` (Java 7+). Should be compatible with modern Java.

```java
  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Reverts the game state to the most recent checkpoint by popping the
   *   top GameStateTransition off the history stack and applying its
   *   reverse() atomically. A finite undo quota is decremented only when a
   *   checkpoint was actually consumed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If undoQuota == 0, do nothing (undo is not allowed when quota is 0).
   *   2. If history is empty, do nothing (quota is not consumed).
   *   3. GameStateTransition last = history.pop();
   *   4. GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
   *   5. For each (to, from) in reversed.moves:
   *        entities.putEntity(to, new Empty());
   *        entities.putEntity(from, entityRecordedInReversedMove);
   *   6. currentTransition = new GameStateTransition();
   *   7. If undoQuota == -1 (unlimited), keep it; else if undoQuota > 0,
   *      decrement by 1.
   * Related Features:
   *   - GameState.history
   *   - GameState.currentTransition (reset to empty)
   *   - GameState.undoQuota
```

```java
public void move(final Position from, final Position to)
{
  Entity entity = getEntities().get(from);
  if (entity instanceof Empty || entity instanceof Wall) {
    return;  // invalid
  }
  Entity destEntity = getEntities().get(to);
  if (!(destEntity instanceof Empty) && destEntity != entity) {
    return;  // invalid
  }
  getEntities().put(from, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
  getEntities().put(to, entity);
  if (getCurrentTransition() != null) {

  }
}
```

**`undo()`**:
```java
public void undo()
{
  if (getUndoQuota() == 0) return;
  if (getHistory().isEmpty()) return;
  GameStateTransition last = getHistory().pop();
  GameStateTransition reversed = last.reverse();
  for (Entry<Position, Position> e : reversed.getMoves().entrySet()) {
    Position to = e.getKey();
    Position from = e.getValue();
    Entity entity = getEntities().get(to);
    getEntities().put(to, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
    getEntities().put(from, entity);
  }
  setCurrentTransition(Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameStateTransition());
  if (getUndoQuota() > 0) {
    setUndoQuota(getUndoQuota() - 1);
  }
}
```

**`getAllPlayerPositions()`**:
```java
public EList<Position> getAllPlayerPositions()
{
  List<Entry<Integer, Position>> players = new ArrayList<Entry<Integer, Position>>();
  for (Entry<Position, Entity> e : getEntities().entrySet()) {
    Entity ent = e.getValue();
    if (ent instanceof Player) {
      players.add(new java.util.AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<Integer, Position>(((Player) ent).getId(), e.getKey()));
    }
  }
  players.sort(new Comparator<Entry<Integer, Position>>() {
    public int compare(Entry<Integer, Position> a, Entry<Integer, Position> b) {
      return Integer.compare(a.getKey(), b.getKey());
    }
  });
  EList<Position> result = new BasicEList<Position>();
  for (Entry<Integer, Position> p : players) {
    result.add(p.getValue());
  }
  return result;
}
```
